novelty.name: Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA): peers as the drift witness, a signature-free TOA

verdict.name: Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA): peers as the drift witness, a signature-free TOA
verdict.closest: CIoTA: Collaborative IoT Anomaly Detection via Blockchain (Golomb, Mirsky, Elovici; NDSS DISS 2018, arXiv 1803.03807; journal version JPDC 145, 2020). Each device keeps a local model, and new behaviour enters only when peers agree (75% element-wise consensus), explicitly so that rare benign events can be told apart from malicious ones. Closest on mechanism: R-DPFL (arXiv 2609.07312, 2026), which takes a robust neighbour aggregate (geometric median allowed) and clips the remainder for each personalised client. Closest on the slogan: LE3D (CCNC 2023), which calls drift shared across neighbouring devices natural and drift on one device abnormal or malicious.
verdict.reasoning:
Three independent search passes found no paper with FOA's full combination: per-device centroid-detector adaptation, a geometric-median peer consensus over each device's proposed shift that is applied in full, only the peer-unexplained residual sent through TOA's cumulative B0+B*t budget, vulnerability-diverse peer groups, a join procedure with a poisoning bound of B0+K*B, and a multi-stream escape from single-stream impossibility results. Both impossibility results were read in full: WARDEN Theorem 15 (arXiv 2607.21673) and Atarmla's blind-set result (arXiv 2609.23254). Both are single-stream and never mention peers or side streams, so the T2 escape is not pre-empted.

The headline idea is still taken, so "novel" would overclaim:
(1) "Peers as the drift witness that gates IoT detector updates" is CIoTA (2018/2020). It accepts new behaviour only on peer consensus, says it separates rare benign events from attacks, and notes that an attacker must compromise p_c of the models.
(2) LE3D already labels common-mode drift natural and single-device drift malicious.
(3) Robust aggregation plus clipping for personalised clients is standard: R-DPFL 2026, ClippedGossip, BALANCE (CCS 2024), BR-MTRL.
(4) Splitting many streams into a common part and a residual is the network-wide PCA subspace method. ANTIDOTE (IMC 2009) showed that this split can be poisoned through the common part.
(5) Vulnerability-diverse replica selection comes from BFT (Lazarus, Middleware 2019).
(6) Starting a new detector from a peer's model is prior art: Cisco US10749768B2, DIoT, and transfer-learning autoencoders.
(7) Byzantine multi-sensor change detection (Fellouris-Bayraktar-Lai 2016; arXiv 1306.2086) already supplies the logic "at most f bad streams makes contamination detectable".

The theory is also weaker than pitched:
- T1 composes the Kloft-Laskov centroid displacement bound with the geometric median's breakdown point of 1/2. It has an unbudgeted per-cycle leak (g*C*sigma_idio) on the consensus channel, which is exactly the frog-boiling attack surface (Chan-Tin et al., SecureComm 2009 / TISSEC 2011). The resulting linear time-to-compromise matches the linear-regret tightness result of Dong et al. 2023.
- T2 is not a corollary of Theorem 15. It changes the observation model and is true more or less by assumption: honest drift is common-mode and contamination reaches at most f streams. TPR -> 1 also needs f/|P| -> 0.
- Vulnerability diversity pushes benign vendor-specific drift, such as a firmware push to one vendor, into the budgeted residual. That opens a liveness gap in T3. Cross-vendor credential botnets and a compromised relay gateway break the f < |P|/2 assumption.

What remains new is the specific budgeted common/residual split, the diverse-peer design point in this setting, the bounded join, and a formal multi-stream escape. That is a real but incremental contribution.
verdict.how_to_differentiate:
1. Reframe the claim. Do not claim "peers as witness". Claim "the first budgeted common/residual update split for label-free detector adaptation, with a multi-stream escape from the drift/contamination ceiling". Cite CIoTA, LE3D and R-DPFL up front.

2. Contrast with CIoTA directly, and show it empirically:
- CIoTA's same-firmware peers absorb a single-exploit campaign as consensus. FOA's vulnerability-diverse peers do not. Run a monoculture-botnet scenario where CIoTA-style same-type consensus fails and FOA holds.
- CIoTA discards anything without consensus. FOA admits that remainder slowly through a budget. Show that this keeps liveness for device-specific benign drift.

3. Prove T2 as a standalone theorem. Use a joint multi-stream two-world construction with fixed f, not a fixed fraction of |P|. Also state the matching negative result: drift that hits only the victim is still indistinguishable, at rates up to about B (cf. Atarmla's Corollary 2). An honest characterisation of where the escape holds is more defensible than a corollary claim.

4. Close the T1 leak. Add a second cumulative budget on the consensus channel, or a cap on the fraction of the cumulative common-mode shift. Prove time-to-compromise under frog-boiling minority collusion with realistic |P| of 5-7, and report the geometric-median constant C empirically at that size.

5. Use the right baselines: WARDEN's frozen-reserve gate (also signature-free), CIoTA-style consensus gating, R-DPFL-style clipped robust aggregation, LE3D's drift labelling, and TOA with a signature. Evaluate on real multi-device traces (N-BaIoT across vendors) with injected common-mode network drift, vendor-specific firmware drift, and a single-vendor botnet.

6. Report the failure boundaries explicitly:
- f >= |P|/2, framed as the ANTIDOTE common-mode poisoning issue.
- Gateway or relay compromise, and cross-vendor credential botnets (Mirai-style).
- Gain g_i amplifying the attacker's bias.

Claim the join bound B0+K*B as an improvement over Cisco/DIoT peer initialisation, and measure it against the 34% new-device false-alarm result.

hits.title: Self-Poisoning in Adaptive Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Sharp-Threshold Theory and Certified Label-Free Calibration (V. B. Balachandran). This is the source of WARDEN and Theorem 15.
hits.year: 2026 (arXiv v1, 23 Jul 2026; preprint, no venue listed)
hits.how_close: This is the impossibility FOA says it escapes, not prior art for FOA. I read the full HTML (both halves). WARDEN is the paper's certified admission gate: it computes conformal p-values against a FROZEN RESERVE with a frozen scorer, gated by e-BH. Theorem 15 covers a single unlabelled score stream: World A is drifted ID P'=(1-pi)P+piQ, World B is P contaminated at rate pi from the ID tail Q, and the ceiling is kappa=alpha/(pi+alpha(1-pi)). The paper never mentions multiple streams, peers, fleets, federated setups or side information as an escape. Its only escapes are labels, a governance cap pi_max, and an unverifiable separation assumption (A2). The 'peers as side information' angle is therefore not in this paper. Caveat for T2: Theorem 15 constrains decision thresholds on a score stream. FOA's corollary would need its own two-world argument over joint multi-stream laws, and it holds only when honest drift is common-mode. Honest drift that hits the victim alone is still indistinguishable from contamination of that one stream. Also, WARDEN's frozen reserve is itself signature-free, so FOA must beat it as a baseline.

hits.title: Robust Decentralized Personalized Federated Learning via Prediction-Constrained Neighborhood Collaboration (R-DPFL; Ma, Shen, Tian, Lyu, Ke)
hits.how_close: The closest mechanism I found. Each client keeps its own personalized model and computes d_bar = RobustAgg(neighbor updates), where RobustAgg can explicitly be a coordinate median, trimmed mean or geometric median. It predicts d_hat from its own history, clips the deviation (d_bar - d_hat) with an EMA-adaptive threshold, and adds the result to its local gradient step. The Byzantine assumption is a fraction below 1/2 per neighbourhood. This is the same pattern as FOA: robust peer aggregate plus a clipped remainder. The differences: the remainder it clips is (peer aggregate - own prediction), not (own update - peer consensus). The clip is per-round and EMA-based, not a cumulative ||sum r|| <= B0+B*t budget. The setting is classifier training on static CIFAR-10 with a Dirichlet split, with no concept drift, no anomaly detector, no poisoning-through-drift threat, no join bound and no vulnerability-diverse peers (verified from the HTML).

hits.title: Online Decentralized Federated Multi-task Learning With Trustworthiness in Cyber-Physical Systems (Odeyomi, Olaosebikan, Opeyemi, Ige)
hits.how_close: Close in setting: peer-to-peer, personalized per-client models, each client's data distribution TIME-VARYING, and Byzantine neighbours that may outnumber honest ones. Robustness comes from trust probabilities derived from cyber-physical side signals such as RSSI, not from a robust statistic. I verified only the abstract and metadata. It does not mention anomaly detection, a consensus/residual split, a cumulative budget or a join procedure. It is prior work for 'robust peer collaboration under drift' in general, but not for using peers to tell drift from poisoning in a detector.

hits.title: Byzantine-Robust Decentralized Federated Learning (BALANCE; Fang, Zhang, Hairi, Khanduri, Liu, Lu, Liu, Gong)
hits.how_close: Each client uses its OWN local model as the reference for accepting or rejecting neighbour models. The trust direction is the reverse of FOA's, which uses the peer consensus as the reference and the self-residual as the suspect. It has convergence guarantees under poisoning. It handles neither drift nor anomaly detection. It is important as a baseline and as evidence that per-client screening of neighbours is established.

hits.title: Byzantine-Robust Decentralized Learning via ClippedGossip (He, Karimireddy, Jaggi)
hits.how_close: Foundation for Byzantine-robust gossip consensus. It compares against a geometric-median baseline and ties robustness to the Byzantine fraction and the graph's spectral gap. The 'gossip Delta and robust-aggregate' step of FOA is standard here. There is no drift or anomaly detection.

hits.title: SketchGuard: Scaling Byzantine-Robust Decentralized Federated Learning via Sketch-Based Screening
hits.how_close: Byzantine screening of neighbours in decentralized FL using compressed sketches. It is relevant to FOA's 10-float gossip budget. I saw only search-result text, not the full paper. It does not address drift or detectors.

hits.title: Byzantine-Robust Distributed Online Learning: Taming Adversarial Participants in An Adversarial Environment (Dong, Wu, Ling, Tian)
hits.year: 2023 (arXiv v3, Dec 2023; the search snippet said IEEE TSP but the arXiv page lists no venue) - BACKGROUND
hits.how_close: Proves that with robust aggregation, distributed online learning under Byzantine attack gets only LINEAR adversarial regret, and that this is tight. Sublinear regret needs i.i.d. honest losses. This bears directly on T1/T3: whatever attack bias passes through the geometric median is applied 'in full' every cycle, so the g*C*sigma_idio term in T1 is an unbudgeted per-cycle leak. FOA's time-to-compromise bound must accept linear growth, which fits this paper's tightness result. It does not handle drift or detectors.

hits.title: Byzantine-Resilient Decentralized Online Resource Allocation
hits.how_close: Decentralized online setting with robust aggregation plus clipping. It gives linear dynamic-regret bounds whose constants depend on the robust aggregator. This is the same form of result as FOA's T3 lag bound. The domain differs (resource allocation, not detection). I saw only search-result text.

hits.title: ANTIDOTE: Understanding and Defending against Poisoning of Anomaly Detectors (Rubinstein, Nelson, Huang, Joseph, Lau, Rao, Taft, Tygar), plus the companion paper 'Stealthy poisoning attacks on PCA-based anomaly detectors'
hits.how_close: A direct foundation for the 'common-mode vs residual across many streams' idea. The network-wide PCA-subspace detector splits traffic into a normal common subspace and a residual subspace. These papers show that boiling-frog chaff poisons that cross-stream decomposition when it is retrained, and they defend with robust PCA. Related work must explain why FOA's peer-consensus channel, which is applied in full, avoids the same fate. FOA's answer is the geometric median plus vulnerability-diverse peers. PDF also found at https://ptolemy.berkeley.edu/projects/truststc/pubs/725/IMC.2009.pdf. Also cite Lakhina et al., 'Diagnosing network-wide traffic anomalies', SIGCOMM 2004 as the base subspace method. I could NOT verify that one this session (ACM returned 403).

hits.title: DÏoT: A Federated Self-learning Anomaly Detection System for IoT (Nguyen, Marchal, Miettinen, Fereidooni, Asokan, Sadeghi)
hits.how_close: Groups IoT devices by type and federates per-type normal-behaviour models. It is the canonical prior use of a device peer group for IoT anomaly detection. It does not split updates into a robust consensus part and a budgeted residual, and it does not reason about drift versus poisoning.

hits.title: Poisoning Attacks on Federated Learning-based IoT Intrusion Detection System (DISS workshop at NDSS)
hits.how_close: Shows that a few compromised IoT devices can gradually poison a DÏoT-style peer-aggregated detector. This is the attack FOA's peer channel has to withstand. Exact authors and venue details were not re-verified this session.

hits.title: Byzantine Fault Tolerant Distributed Quickest Change Detection
hits.year: 2013 (SIAM J. Control Optim., per the search snippet) - BACKGROUND
hits.how_close: Multiple sensors watch one process and an unknown subset is compromised. Plain CUSUM breaks with even one dishonest sensor, and a distributed scheme recovers log-scaling delay. This is the classical form of 'other streams act as a robust change witness' and should be cited next to T2. It does not cover adaptation, budgets or IoT detectors.

hits.title: Lazarus: Automatic Management of Diversity in BFT Systems (Garcia, Bessani, Neves)
hits.how_close: Chooses BFT replicas so they share no vulnerabilities, using NVD feeds, because the f-out-of-n assumption needs independent failures. This is direct precedent for FOA's 'vulnerability-diverse peer group' rationale, so cite it rather than claim it as new. The earlier DSN 2011 paper 'OS diversity for intrusion tolerance: Myth or reality?' was only seen as a citation in other work.

hits.title: CARVY-FL: Client Anticlustering for Robust Voting in Provably Secure Federated Learning (Nakada et al.)
hits.how_close: Forms groups to maximise diversity within each group (anticlustering) for robust certified voting. The diversity is over data distribution, not vendor or firmware. It has no correlated-compromise model, no drift and no anomaly detection. It is a weak analogue of FOA's diverse peer selection.

hits.title: FLARE: Detection and Mitigation of Concept Drift for Federated Learning based IoT Deployments
hits.how_close: Detects concept drift in federated IoT with a KS test and explicitly notes that drift may come from data poisoning. It does not separate the two. It confirms the gap rather than closing it.

hits.title: Hybrid Intrusion Detection System with Real-Time Concept Drift Detection for Enhanced IoT Security (Sensors, MDPI)
hits.how_close: Keeps drift detection apart from retraining and says safe online retraining needs poisoning protection and update validation, which it leaves as future work. This confirms the gap. Mirror: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13517801/

hits.title: Heterogeneity-Aware Poisoning Attacks and Mitigation in Federated Learning: A Comprehensive Survey and Taxonomy (Electronics, MDPI)
hits.how_close: Survey that states the core tension: benign non-IID drift can be misclassified as malicious, and adaptive poisoning can hide inside widened benign variation. It confirms the problem FOA targets and offers no peer-consensus/residual-budget mechanism. I saw only search-result text.

hits.title: Transfer Learning Auto-Encoder Neural Networks for Anomaly Detection of DDoS Generating IoT Devices
hits.year: 2022 (per the search summary; venue not verified)
hits.how_close: Starts a new IoT device's detector from a similar device's model, which is partial prior art for FOA's Join step. It assumes the source is clean and has no poisoning bound like B0+K*B.

hits.title: Cato CTRL: Advanced Behavioral Analysis of IoT and OT Devices for IoC Collection (Cato Networks blog; industry, not peer-reviewed)
hits.how_close: Shows that per-device plus peer-group baselining of IoT/OT devices is commercial practice for DETECTION. It does not use peers to gate detector ADAPTATION. Worth one line so reviewers do not claim 'peer groups are novel'.

hits.title: Adversarial Concept Drift Detection under Poisoning Attacks for Robust Data Stream Mining
hits.year: 2020 preprint; later in the Machine Learning journal (PMC9162121, 2022) - BACKGROUND
hits.how_close: Single-stream: a trainable RBM detector separates real drift from adversarial drift. It uses no peers. It is the single-stream baseline that FOA's multi-stream argument goes beyond.

hits.conclusion:
I could not kill FOA. No paper I found does the full combination: per-device anomaly-detector adaptation, a geometric median over a peer group used as the drift witness, the whole consensus part applied, only the residual run through a cumulative budget, peers chosen to be vulnerability-diverse, and a bounded join for new devices. The WARDEN paper (arXiv 2607.21673, 2026) is single-stream, and I read its full text: it never offers multiple streams or peers as an escape from Theorem 15.

Every component has precedent, though, so the novelty has to rest on the combination and the theorems:
(a) Robust aggregation of neighbour updates, with each client keeping a personalized model, is established. See ClippedGossip 2022, BALANCE (CCS 2024), SketchGuard 2025 and arXiv 2509.00992 (2025, time-varying data). The closest mechanism is R-DPFL (arXiv 2609.07312, 2026), which takes a robust neighbour aggregate (geometric median allowed) and clips the remainder, but per round and EMA-based, with no drift and no detector.
(b) Splitting many streams into a common-mode part and a residual is the network-wide PCA subspace method. ANTIDOTE (IMC 2009) showed boiling-frog poisoning of exactly that decomposition.
(c) Vulnerability-diverse replica selection comes from BFT (Lazarus, Middleware 2019).
(d) Device-type peer models for IoT anomaly detection come from DÏoT (ICDCS 2019).
(e) Byzantine-robust distributed change detection exists (arXiv 1306.2086).

Technical risks that reviewers will raise:
1. T1 has an unbudgeted leak. The attacker's bias passes through the median and is applied in full every cycle. That makes compromise time linear, in line with the tightness result in Dong et al. 2023. With realistic small peer groups (|P| around 5-7), the geometric-median constant C grows without bound as f/|P| approaches 1/2. Bounding by sigma_idio also assumes honest deltas are tightly concentrated.
2. T2 is not a corollary of Theorem 15 as written. Theorem 15 is about one label-free score stream. FOA needs its own two-world argument over joint multi-stream laws. It holds only for common-mode honest drift: drift that hits the victim alone is still indistinguishable from contamination. 'TPR -> 1 as |P| grows' needs f fixed (or f/|P| -> 0), not a fixed fraction.
3. Vulnerability diversity is weak against credential-based botnets (Mirai-style) that cross vendors. A gateway that relays the gossip is a single point where all peers can be compromised at once, and the HMAC proves only who sent an update, not that it is honest.
4. The per-device gain g_i is fitted in warm-up and could amplify the attacker's bias.
5. WARDEN's frozen-reserve gate is also signature-free, so it must be a baseline.

Coverage caveat: the shared web-search budget ran out after about 20 searches, so later checks used direct fetches only. Areas not yet searched: multi-stream adversarial-drift papers, smart-meter and UEBA peer-group adaptation, and drift compensation by collaborative or common-PCA calibration in sensor networks. A follow-up message can resume the search. Some entries are verified only from search snippets, and each one is flagged.

hits.title: CIoTA: Collaborative IoT Anomaly Detection via Blockchain (Golomb, Mirsky, Elovici; NDSS DISS workshop 2018)
hits.how_close: Closest mechanism I found, read in full text. Devices of the same type each keep a local model. New behaviour enters the shared model only if enough peers agree: the paper says it accepts 'new states to the EMM only when there is a consensus among the models'. Concretely, a combined model keeps only elements present in at least pc=75% of L=20 signed peer models. The authors say this lets it tell 'rare benign events' apart from malicious ones, and an attacker 'must compromise at least pc of the models'. So peer consensus as the gate for benign novelty versus local poisoning is already published. What it does NOT have, and FOA does: (1) Peers are the same model and firmware, with one chain per firmware, so a single-exploit campaign is common-mode and gets absorbed. That is exactly the failure FOA's vulnerability-diverse peer group is meant to avoid. (2) It replaces the local model with the consensus; there is no per-device model that keeps a residual under a cumulative budget. (3) It models control-flow memory jumps (Markov chains), not traffic centroids. (4) No drift-rate or liveness analysis, no theorems, no bound on how much a joining device can be poisoned. FOA must cite and contrast this.

hits.title: LE3D: A Lightweight Ensemble Framework of Data Drift Detectors for Resource-Constrained Devices (Mavromatis et al., IEEE CCNC 2023)
hits.how_close: Already publishes the 'peers as drift witness' slogan. Drift seen across several neighbouring devices with the same sensor type is classed as 'natural'; drift on one device's stream is 'abnormal', which 'can be considered malicious'. Devices share votes and a one-sample KS statistic with neighbours. Read in full text (ar5iv), it is detection only. It never adapts a model with the split, assumes no compromised or Byzantine neighbours, uses no robust aggregation across devices, gives no bounds, and its cross-device rule is qualitative. It weakens the novelty of the idea in words, not of FOA's budgeted-residual mechanism or its theorems.

hits.title: Self-Poisoning in Adaptive Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Sharp-Threshold Theory and Certified Label-Free Calibration (Balachandran) -- the WARDEN / Theorem 15 paper
hits.how_close: This is the impossibility result FOA says it escapes. I checked the HTML: Theorem 15 builds two worlds (benign tail drift vs. contamination from the same tail law) that give identical unlabelled score streams. Any label-free threshold rule with FPR <= alpha in World A therefore has TPR <= alpha/(pi + alpha(1-pi)) in World B. It is strictly a single-stream result: one window plus a frozen reserve. The paper never mentions multiple streams, peers, fleets or cross-device data, so FOA's escape is not pre-empted. Caveat: it is a result about calibrating label-free OOD thresholds, so FOA's T2 changes the observation model and is a separate theorem, not a corollary of Theorem 15.

hits.title: The Price of Self-Calibration: Exact Evidence Budgets and Manufactured Blind Sets in Adaptive Monitoring (Atarmla)
hits.how_close: A second single-stream impossibility that FOA should cite. A monitor built to tolerate a drift class D is blind to every fault in D - D. For drift whose speed is bounded by v, the blind set is exactly the 2v-speed class (Corollary 2). I checked the HTML: one observation stream, no auxiliary streams or peers. This bears on FOA's residual budget. On the victim's own stream, a residual of speed up to about B (or 2B) stays invisible, which is why T1 only gives a linear-time bound. FOA beats this result only for the common-mode part.

hits.title: Poisoning Attacks on Federated Learning-based IoT Intrusion Detection System (Nguyen, Rieger, Miettinen, Sadeghi; NDSS DISS workshop 2020)
hits.how_close: Defines the threat FOA targets: compromised IoT devices gradually inject small amounts of traffic to poison device-type-specific FL detectors, and the attack beats clustering and clipping/noise defenses. I read the full text. Its mitigation section lists only better server-side FL defenses, filtering poisoned data on the client, and better detection at injection time. Nothing on splitting updates by peer consensus or budgeting the residual. Not a kill.

hits.title: DIoT: A Federated Self-learning Anomaly Detection System for IoT (Nguyen, Marchal, Miettinen, Fereidooni, Asokan, Sadeghi; ICDCS 2019)
hits.how_close: Builds device-type profiles by federated learning, so a new device inherits its type's profile, which is close to FOA's join-from-peer-median step. No defense against gradual poisoning, no drift/attack split, no budgeted join.

hits.title: CADeSH: Collaborative Anomaly Detection for Smart Homes (Meidan, Avraham, Libhaber, Shabtai)
hits.year: arXiv 2023; search snippet says IEEE IoT Journal 2022 (venue/year not directly verified)
hits.how_close: Computes features over a pool of identical devices in different homes to cut false positives, and claims to mitigate model poisoning. Pooling peers fits FOA's motivation, but it has no per-cycle consensus/residual split, no budget and no theory.

hits.title: ANTIDOTE: Understanding and Defending against Poisoning of Anomaly Detectors (Rubinstein et al., ACM IMC 2009)
hits.how_close: Title confirmed from the PDF. A PCA-subspace detector, where the common-mode network-wide subspace counts as normal and the residual as anomalous, is poisoned boiling-frog style by adding chaff across many flows. This is the direct analogue of FOA's declared failure mode: a common-mode signal across many streams gets absorbed. FOA should present its f >= |P|/2 boundary as this known issue.

hits.title: Security Analysis of Online Centroid Anomaly Detection (Kloft, Laskov; JMLR 13, 2012)
hits.how_close: Basis for TOA/FOA's T1: bounds on how far an attacker can push an online centroid detector when it controls only part of the traffic or under an FPR limit. The search results show no multi-stream or peer-consensus defense. T1 is essentially this bound combined with the geometric median's 1/2 breakdown point.

hits.title: Efficient Byzantine Sequential Change Detection (Fellouris, Bayraktar, Lai)
hits.how_close: Detects changes across many sensors when up to a known number may be adversarial, with worst-case delay and false-alarm guarantees. A formal precedent for the logic of T2 ('at most f bad streams makes it detectable'), with the framing reversed: there the common change is the event to detect, in FOA the common change is benign drift. FOA should cite it for multi-stream robustness.

hits.title: Resilient Distributed Diffusion in Networks with Adversaries (Li, Abbas, Koutsoukos; IEEE TSIPN 2020)
hits.how_close: Agents estimate stationary or non-stationary parameters from neighbours; the paper shows attacks that steer them, plus a resilient algorithm that works if each neighbourhood has a bounded number of compromised agents, with an MSD/resilience trade-off. Analogous to FOA's T1 plus T3 (tracking under bounded compromised peers). It is not anomaly detection and has no budget on the residual.

hits.title: Lazarus: Automatic Management of Diversity in BFT Systems (Garcia, Bessani, Neves; ACM Middleware 2019)
hits.how_close: Picks replicas that do not share vulnerabilities, using vulnerability data, so one exploit cannot break more than f. Direct precedent for FOA's vulnerability-diverse peer group (same idea from BFT replication); it should be cited as the source of that design choice.

hits.title: Byzantine Resilient Federated Multi-Task Representation Learning (BR-MTRL) (Le, Moothedath)
hits.how_close: Same structure: the shared part is aggregated robustly (geometric median or Krum) while each client keeps a personal part (its own final layer). Server-based supervised learning, with no drift, no cumulative budget on the personal part, no anomaly detection and no join bound. Moderate, structural similarity only.

hits.title: Decentralized Federated Learning towards Communication Efficiency, Robustness, and Personalization (D-CERP) (Zhang, Zhao, Lu, Zhang; ACM TOSN 21(3))
hits.how_close: Decentralized personalized FL that picks trusted neighbours with a bandit to resist Byzantine peers. Tested on images only; no drift/attack split, no budget. Weak.

hits.title: Byzantine-Robust Decentralized Learning via ClippedGossip (He, Karimireddy, Jaggi)
hits.how_close: Robust gossip that clips neighbour differences, the closest standard mechanism to FOA's steps 3-5. It trains one consensus model with no per-device detector, no drift handling and no cumulative residual budget.

hits.title: Byzantine-Robust Gossip: Insights from a Dual Approach (Gaucher, Dieuleveut, Hendrikx)
hits.how_close: Robust decentralized averaging/learning with convergence guarantees. Could replace FOA's consensus step; nothing on drift, anomaly detection or budgets.

hits.title: Ditto: Fair and Robust Federated Learning Through Personalization (Li, Hu, Beirami, Smith; ICML 2021)
hits.how_close: Personal models regularized toward a global model resist poisoning. Shares the idea of a personal model anchored to a robust common part; nothing on drift or the residual budget.

hits.title: Robustness and Personalization in Federated Learning: A Unified Approach via Regularization (Fed+) (Kundu, Yu, Wynter, Lim; IEEE EDGE 2022)
hits.how_close: Personal local models plus robust server aggregation (a search snippet mentions geometric-median and clipped variants; I did not verify that in the full text). Weak to moderate.

hits.title: Adaptive Federated Learning Defense Against Byzantine Attacks and Concept Drift in IIoT (Alhelou, Singh, Wang; IEEE ISCAS 2026, in press)
hits.how_close: Handles both Byzantine clients and concept drift, but by switching from FedAvg to a robust aggregator when it detects attacks or drift. Centralized, global model, no consensus/residual split. Details are not verified: the repository refused my connection, so I only saw the search snippet.

hits.title: CrowdGuard: Federated Backdoor Detection in Federated Learning (Rieger, Krauss, Miettinen, Dmitrienko, Sadeghi; NDSS 2024)
hits.how_close: Clients check other clients' models on their own data (hidden-layer analysis, inside TEEs, with server-side clustering). It uses peers to vet updates, but for backdoor detection in centralized FL, not drift-split adaptation. Weak.

hits.title: Contrastive Adversarial Agents for Intentional Drift Induction in Network Intrusion Detection Systems (Rivas, Piplai; AAAI Spring Symposium)
hits.how_close: Attack side: deliberately induces drift to break NIDS retraining. Supports FOA's threat model; offers no peer-based defense.

hits.title: Online Drift Correction in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Spatio-Temporal Modeling (Takruri et al., UTS)
hits.how_close: Each sensor predicts its reading from its neighbours' readings to correct its own drift, assuming drift on one sensor is uncorrelated with the others. Same 'neighbours as reference' logic in sensor calibration; no adversary.

hits.title: Personalized federated learning-based intrusion detection system: Poisoning attack and defense (Thein, Shiraishi, Morii; Future Generation Computer Systems)
hits.year: 2024 (only the title and venue seen in a search snippet; content NOT verified, URL not found)
hits.how_close: Possibly relevant (personalized FL-IDS plus a poisoning defense), but my web search budget ran out before I could open it. Needs a manual check.

hits.conclusion:
I could not kill FOA, but parts of it are not new. No paper I found combines all of these: a per-device adaptive centroid detector; a robust peer consensus (geometric median) over each device's per-cycle proposed shift; applying the peer-backed part in full and only the leftover through a cumulative budget; peers chosen for differing vulnerabilities; a bounded join for new devices; and theorems that escape single-stream impossibility results.

What already exists and must be cited:
(1) CIoTA (2018) already lets new behaviour into per-device-type models only when peers agree, specifically so rare benign events are not mistaken for attacks. That is the closest prior work.
(2) LE3D (2022/23) already labels drift shared across neighbouring same-type devices as natural and single-device drift as abnormal. So 'peers as the drift witness' is not new as an idea.

FOA's real differences:
(a) Applying the consensus part in full while the residual is budgeted, instead of replacing the local model or only detecting.
(b) Vulnerability-diverse peers instead of same-firmware peers. CIoTA's same-firmware design is exactly the single-exploit common-mode case FOA avoids; the idea comes from BFT work (Lazarus 2019).
(c) The join bound B0 + K*B.
(d) The safety, escape and liveness theorems.

Theory check:
- WARDEN's Theorem 15 (arXiv 2607.21673) and Atarmla's blind-set result (arXiv 2609.23254) are both single-stream by construction. I checked both texts: neither mentions peers or auxiliary streams, so the escape is not pre-empted.
- T2 should not be called a corollary of Theorem 15. It changes the observation model, from one unlabelled stream to several, with a control group. The argument is close to standard multi-sensor Byzantine detection (Fellouris, Bayraktar, Lai 2016).
- T1 and T3 are mostly Kloft-Laskov-style displacement bounds combined with the geometric median's 1/2 breakdown point, plus resilient-diffusion tracking (Li, Abbas, Koutsoukos 2020). Present them as modest compositions, not deep results.
- On the victim's own stream, a residual drifting at up to about B (or 2B) is still invisible, per Atarmla's Corollary 2. T1 is therefore only a linear-time bound.

Failure boundary: the declared f >= |P|/2 limit is the known ANTIDOTE (IMC 2009) common-mode poisoning issue and should be framed that way. Add one more case: a network-level campaign that reaches all peers at once (shared gateway compromise, or scanning or injection that hits every device in the same role) is common-mode and is applied in full, whatever the vendor diversity.

Not verified: Thein et al. (FGCS 2024) and the details of the ISCAS 2026 Essex paper. My web search budget ran out (200 searches per turn) before I could open them; a follow-up message can continue the search.

hits.title: CIoTA: Collaborative IoT Anomaly Detection via Blockchain (Golomb, Mirsky, Elovici; NDSS 2018 DISS workshop)
hits.how_close: CLOSEST on the core principle. I read the full text. Each IoT device keeps a local anomaly model (an EMM over control-flow jumps), and new benign behaviour enters the shared model only when peers agree. The paper says it accepts new states 'only when there is a consensus among the models' (element-wise threshold p_c = 75%), and that an attacker 'must compromise at least p_c of the models' to evade detection. It claims to 'differentiate between rare benign events and malicious activities' by using 'the wisdom of the many'. So 'peers as the drift witness, with updates accepted only when peers back them' already exists. Differences from FOA: (1) peers are the SAME device model and firmware, the opposite of FOA's vulnerability-diverse groups, so a single-exploit campaign is common-mode for CIoTA; (2) behaviour without consensus is dropped, not passed through a cumulative slow budget; (3) it uses a discrete element-wise vote, with no geometric median and no continuous centroid; (4) no theory (no time-to-compromise bound, no breakdown analysis, no impossibility link); (5) no join protocol. FOA has to cite this and set itself apart from it explicitly.

hits.title: Lightweight Collaborative Anomaly Detection for the IoT using Blockchain (Mirsky, Golomb, Elovici; J. Parallel and Distributed Computing vol. 145, 2020)
hits.how_close: The journal extension of CIoTA. It keeps the same idea: same-type devices merge their models and new behaviour is filtered by consensus. Venue and volume come from search snippets. I did not read the full text, so I cannot say whether it adds budgets or drift theory.

hits.title: Self-Poisoning in Adaptive Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Sharp-Threshold Theory and Certified Label-Free Calibration (WARDEN / CDC; V. B. Balachandran)
hits.year: 2026 (arXiv preprint, July 2026; no peer review found)
hits.how_close: This is the impossibility result FOA claims to escape, not a kill. I read the HTML. Theorem 15 sets World A, where the ID law drifts to (1-pi)P + piQ, against World B, where each point is independently replaced by a draw from Q (the ID tail) with probability pi. The two give identical unlabelled stream laws, so FPR_A <= alpha forces TPR_B <= alpha/(pi + alpha(1-pi)). The paper never mentions peers, multiple streams or cross-device side information. The only escape it names is labels, which 'break the tie'. Its Limitations section lists a one-dimensional state model and single-stream experiments. FOA's T2 (peers as side information) is therefore not anticipated here. T2 is safe from prior art, but it rests entirely on the assumption that drift is common-mode while contamination is not.

hits.title: The Frog-Boiling Attack: Limitations of Anomaly Detection for Secure Network Coordinate Systems (Chan-Tin, Feldman, Hopper, Kim; SecureComm 2009; extended in ACM TISSEC 14(3), 2011)
hits.how_close: A peer-based update system where each node moves using neighbours' reports. Outlier filtering of peer inputs (Mahalanobis, Kalman) is defeated by 'small-step' consistent lies that stay under the threshold. Roughly 5-11% attackers is enough, and the authors conclude 'outlier detection alone cannot be used'. This hits FOA's consensus channel: a_i = g_i*m_t is applied IN FULL with no cumulative cap. A minority of f < |P|/2 colluding peers can bias the geometric median by up to about C*sigma_idio per cycle, always in the same direction. FOA's T1 does count this, because the bound is linear in (B + g*C*sigma_idio). But the paper has to show that the median-bias term is small in practice, or add a budget on the common channel too. This is not prior work on FOA itself, but it is the attack reviewers will raise.

hits.title: Poisoning Attacks on Federated Learning-based IoT Intrusion Detection System (Nguyen et al.; NDSS 2020 DISS workshop)
hits.how_close: Shows that compromised IoT devices injecting small amounts of malicious data can backdoor a device-type-federated IoT anomaly detector (DIoT) and evade the standard FL poisoning defences of the time. This is direct evidence that peer-pooled IoT detectors can be poisoned from inside the fleet. It is a threat model FOA must answer, not a version of FOA. Details are from search snippets; I did not read the full text.

hits.title: DIoT: A Federated Self-learning Anomaly Detection System for IoT (Nguyen et al.)
hits.how_close: Device-type-specific anomaly models pooled across deployments with federated learning, so peers are again grouped by device type. There is no common-mode/residual split, no budget and no drift-vs-attack theory. Related only through the 'peer pooling' design.

hits.title: Robust Unsupervised Network Intrusion Detection via Federated Learning with Selective Aggregation under Anomalous Sample Contamination (Kamiguchi, Nishio)
hits.how_close: Moderate. Unsupervised NIDS in a federated setting. An EM step drops client groups whose models diverge from the majority, so contamination on a minority of clients is suppressed. This is 'majority as witness' for label-free AD, but it is batch training (the abstract shows no online drift tracking), it does not split common-mode from residual, it has no budget, and it gives no guarantees.

hits.title: FedPoisonTTP: A Threat Model and Poisoning Attack for Federated Test-Time Personalization (Iftee et al.)
hits.how_close: Related threat. In federated test-time adaptation, where clients adapt on unlabelled streams and share updates, a compromised participant injects in-distribution poisons that spread through the collaborative updates. Attack only, no defence. It shows that 'collaborative label-free adaptation' is an open attack surface, which supports FOA's motivation but also points to the attacker it must face.

hits.title: Robust Federated Personalised Mean Estimation for the Gaussian Mixture Model (Managoli, Prabhakaran, Diggavi)
hits.how_close: Theory neighbour of T1. Each client estimates its own mean with help from peers while a constant fraction of clients are corrupted. Error scales almost linearly with the corrupted/uncorrupted ratio, with a matching lower bound. The setting is static: no drift, no online updates, no budget. It could inform how tightly the consensus error bound C*sigma_idio can be stated.

hits.title: Robust Aggregation for Federated Learning (RFA; Pillutla, Kakade, Harchaoui; IEEE Trans. Signal Processing 2022)
hits.how_close: Source of the smoothed-Weiszfeld geometric-median aggregator FOA uses, and of its breakdown point of 1/2. It covers model aggregation only, not anomaly-detector drift. Cite it for step 3 and for T1's breakdown claim.

hits.title: Unified Breakdown Analysis for Byzantine Robust Gossip (Gaucher et al.; ICML 2025)
hits.how_close: Building block for FOA's gossip layer (ESP-NOW). It gives breakdown analysis for robust aggregation over sparse communication graphs and a new attack aimed at decentralized communication. Relevant if P(i) is reached by gossip rather than through a gateway. It does not address anomaly detection or drift. Venue confirmed via the ICML 2025 listing in search results.

hits.title: ANTIDOTE: Understanding and Defending against Poisoning of Anomaly Detectors (Rubinstein et al.; ACM IMC 2009)
hits.how_close: The original 'boiling frog' poisoning of network-wide PCA (subspace) detectors. That detector already splits a common normal subspace shared across links from a residual. The paper explicitly notes the learner's 'inability to distinguish between benign data drift and adversarial poisoning'. This is the classic multi-stream common-plus-residual detector, and it was shown poisonable through the common part. FOA is the inverse design (the common part is trusted, the residual is budgeted). Reviewers will raise this precedent.

hits.title: Can't Boil This Frog: Robustness of Online-Trained Autoencoder-Based Anomaly Detectors to Adversarial Poisoning Attacks (Kravchik, Biggio, Shabtai)
hits.how_close: Single-stream gradual poisoning of online-retrained ICS detectors. It motivates the problem but uses no peers. Not a kill.

hits.title: Adversarial Concept Drift Detection under Poisoning Attacks for Robust Data Stream Mining (Korycki, Krawczyk; Machine Learning journal, 2022)
hits.how_close: Single stream. It separates instance-based poisoning from concept-based poisoning that imitates real drift, and builds a drift detector robust to poisoning. There is no peer or multi-stream witness. It supports the single-stream hardness claim but does not do FOA.

hits.title: Localized fault-tolerant event boundary detection in sensor networks (IEEE INFOCOM 2005)
hits.how_close: Classic WSN neighbour-consensus logic: real events are spatially correlated across neighbours, while faults are 'geographically independent'. This is the same common-mode vs idiosyncratic split, used for fault vs event, with no adversary and no budget. It shows that 'peers as witness' is an old principle. I did not verify the author list.

hits.title: A mapping method for anomaly detection in a localized population of structures (Lin et al.; Data-Centric Engineering, Cambridge)
hits.how_close: Population-based monitoring of a wind farm. It models correlations between turbines so that shared environmental and operating variation is explained by the population, and anomalies are the unexplained part. Same fleet-as-baseline idea in a non-adversarial domain. Not security, and no budget.

hits.title: Using a multi-network dataset to overcome anomaly detection cold starts (Cisco; US Patent 10749768B2)
hits.how_close: Close to FOA step 6 (Join). A new network starts with the anomaly detector of the most similar existing network, runs in an announced 'cold start mode', and moves to its own model after two weeks to two months. The part I read says nothing about poisoning or a bounded join-time budget. FOA's 'start at the peer median and budget the residual for K cycles, giving the bound B0 + K*B' is still a new twist, but the peer-initialization idea itself has prior art.

hits.title: HIoT: heterogeneous information network based compromised IoT device detection (Cybersecurity, Springer)
hits.how_close: Counter-evidence for FOA's assumptions. Its premise is that devices compromised by the same attack show correlated behaviour (shared C2 infrastructure). That means a campaign IS common-mode among devices with the same vulnerability, which is why FOA needs vulnerability-diverse peers. Details are from a search snippet only; not read in full.

hits.title: When Normality Shifts: Risk-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for Unsupervised Tabular Anomaly Detection (RTTAD; Huang et al.)
hits.how_close: Weak. Single-model, single-stream label-free test-time adaptation that updates on high-confidence pseudo-normals to avoid contamination. No peers, no budget theory. A baseline to compare against, not a kill.

hits.title: Anomaly Detection for IoT Global Connectivity (ANCHOR; Omaña Iglesias et al., Telefónica)
hits.how_close: Weak. Flags anomalies at the level of a client's whole IoT fleet. No security, poisoning or drift-adaptation content in the abstract.

hits.title: Synthetic Anomaly Monitoring (SAM): synthetic-control-based anomaly detection
hits.how_close: Weak. It uses synthetic control as a counterfactual baseline, but the control units are features, not peer devices. There is no drift-vs-attack treatment.

hits.title: Drift-to-Action Controllers: Budgeted Interventions with Online Risk Certificates (Lamaakal et al.; ICLR 2026 CAO workshop)
hits.how_close: Weak. 'Budgeted' here means label, compute and latency costs plus cooldowns. It has no cumulative displacement budget, no poisoning and no peers.

hits.title: Byzantine-robust distributed online learning (Dong, Wu, Ling, Tian)
hits.year: UNVERIFIED (the page returned 403; known only from a search snippet)
hits.how_close: Theory context for T1 and T3. With Byzantine participants in an adversarial environment, robust-aggregation online gradient descent only reaches LINEAR adversarial regret, and the bound is tight. Sublinear regret needs i.i.d. honest losses. This agrees with FOA giving a linear time-to-compromise rather than immunity. Venue and arXiv ID not verified.

hits.conclusion:
I could not kill the idea, but its framing has to shrink. No paper I found (2018 to Oct 2026) combines FOA's three parts: (a) splitting each device's online detector update into a geometric-median peer-consensus part that is applied in full and a peer-unexplained residual that goes through a cumulative B0 + B*t budget, (b) a signature-free time-to-compromise bound, and (c) using peer streams as side information to escape a single-stream drift-vs-contamination impossibility. I read WARDEN (arXiv 2607.21673, July 2026) in full HTML. Theorem 15 is single-stream, the paper never mentions peers or multiple streams, and the only escape it names is labels. So T2 as a corollary is not taken.

What is already taken, and must not be claimed as new:
1. 'Peers as the drift witness for IoT anomaly models' is CIoTA (NDSS DISS 2018; JPDC 2020). Same-type devices accept new benign behaviour into the shared model only on peer consensus (75% element-wise), the attacker must compromise p_c of the models, and the paper says this tells rare benign events apart from malicious activity. FOA's real differences are: vulnerability-diverse rather than same-type peers, budgeting the residual instead of discarding it, a continuous geometric median, formal bounds, and a join protocol.
2. Splitting common-mode from idiosyncratic behaviour by peer comparison is old in non-adversarial settings: WSN fault-vs-event detection (INFOCOM 2005) and population-based structural health monitoring (Data-Centric Engineering 2022).
3. Network-wide common-subspace-plus-residual detection exists and was shown poisonable (ANTIDOTE, IMC 2009).
4. Starting a new deployment from a similar peer's detector is prior art (Cisco US10749768B2). The bounded join-poisoning budget is not.

Risks the literature points to:
(i) The frog-boiling attack (SecureComm 2009 / TISSEC 2011): 5-11% colluding peers telling small, consistent lies defeat outlier-filtered peer updates. FOA applies a_i in full with no cumulative cap, so a minority can push about C*sigma_idio per cycle in a fixed direction. T1 counts this linearly, but the paper must show empirically that it is small, or budget the common channel too.
(ii) Evidence that campaigns are common-mode among same-vulnerability devices (HIoT 2025), and that DIoT-style peer-pooled IoT detectors can be poisoned from inside (NDSS DISS 2020). Both make vulnerability-diverse peer selection essential. But the same diversity turns benign VENDOR-specific drift (for example, a firmware update pushed to one vendor) into idiosyncratic residual, which then hits the slow budget and causes lag or false alarms. This liveness gap in T3 should be reported alongside f >= |P|/2.
(iii) T2's escape follows directly from its assumption: it holds only because drift is assumed common-mode and contamination limited to f streams. Reviewers will want that assumption tested on real multi-device traces.
(iv) Byzantine distributed online learning has a linear adversarial-regret lower bound (Dong et al., venue unverified). That matches FOA offering only a delay, not immunity.

Recommended novelty claim: 'a budgeted common/residual split with vulnerability-diverse peers and the first multi-stream escape from the label-free drift/contamination ceiling'. Not 'peers as witness'.

Coverage caveat: the shared web-search budget (200 calls) ran out partway through. I did not search UEBA peer-group analysis (Bolton and Hand style), W-MSR resilient consensus, attack-resilient sensor fusion, Lakhina's subspace method, or OWAD (NDSS 2023). I did not check if any 2025-2026 paper applies W-MSR-style resilient consensus to IoT detector drift. Some details (HIoT, P4P, Dong et al., Nguyen 2020, the Mirsky JPDC version) come from search snippets only and are marked as such. A follow-up message can resume the search.

novelty.name: Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding: the two-horned attack class on drift-gated defences, with a safety-plus-liveness contract

verdict.name: Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding: the two-horned attack class on drift-gated defences, with a safety-plus-liveness contract
verdict.reasoning:
Nobody has done the whole package. Across three search runs, no paper models an attacker who deliberately trips a suspicion, rollback or stop gate for tau cycles at a cost c(tau) and profits after leaving, when honest drift has made the frozen model stale. No paper states a safety-plus-liveness contract for self-learning detectors, gives a positive result for directional refusal, or attacks the named NIDS defences by tripping their gates. But most of the theory and several of the attack concepts are already published, so this is not "novel".

Already covered:
(1) The static core of the "both horns" theorem. CAPTURE (arXiv:2609.02265), Theorem 2, proves FUR + RRL >= 1 - delta_phi for any rule that reads one statistic: it either accepts injected claims or rejects genuine revisions. That is the single-stream gate dilemma in Le Cam two-point form. It also argues that a rule which looks at history is never worse, which echoes the corollary.
(2) The non-adversarial version of both horns. arXiv:2609.23254 Remark 4 ("no free tuning"): slower adaptation narrows the blind set only at the price of longer miscalibration after legitimate changes. That is the liveness cost, without an attacker. Its Theorem 4 and Corollary 3 give the D-D / 2v blind set, which is the absorb horn.
(3) The safety horn and the two-world construction. arXiv:2607.21673 (WARDEN/CDC), Theorem 15, which the idea builds on. The same paper's Appendix D.2 shows empirically that mimicry makes the dictionary starve and fall back to the base channel, which is an untheorised trip horn. It separately reports 1.94x nominal FPR under drift, but never joins the two findings.
(4) The blinding dual is weakened. WARDEN itself documents that CDC sets tau = +infinity when the level goes above 1, calls it "trivially valid", and says in Corollary 10 that an adversary can suppress the dictionary channel (a power effect). Bashari, Sesia & Romano (ICML 2025) prove that contaminated calibration makes conformal detection conservative and costs power. Kloft & Laskov warn that a learned radius can be poisoned. ANTIDOTE and Bhattacharjee et al. (CPSS 2022) poison learned thresholds.
(5) The attack concepts. Korycki & Krawczyk (2020 / Machine Learning 2022) already name, in prose, "impairing the adaptation process" up to "complete nullification", forcing false adaptation, and draining the labelling budget with fake-novel points. So "freeze adaptation" and "flood the DriftXpert label queue" are not new ideas. Kloft & Laskov (2010) define the switch-off gate that fires on a false-positive threshold and explicitly leave red-herring attacks out of scope, which supports the gap.

Factual problems to fix before claiming "six published defences":
- T2T is verified (Hu & Duan, ICML 2026: the 2.5x mean-of-5 rule and the rollback to w_{t-2}). The paper notes "total loss of utility" under pervasive rejection; cite that.
- RTTAD's stop rule is verified ("until no sufficient samples remain"), but "sufficient" is undefined, and RTTAD is a tabular method, not a traffic one.
- ACORN-IDS computes mu + 2*sigma on a CLEAN held-out split. Stream inflation does not apply unless the attacker can influence that split or the pseudo-labels.
- DriftXpert's identity was confirmed in one run and not in another, and its released code is reportedly incomplete (GitHub issue #1).
- LID box, CB-RBM and RPS could not be verified. The detector in Korycki & Krawczyk is called RRBM-DD.
- EATA and RTTAD are per-sample filters, so freezing them needs honest drift itself to reach the refusal region. That is the corollary's own condition.

Still unsearched, where a direct kill could hide:
- adversarial quickest-change detection (CUSUM false-alarm or delay attacks);
- "framing honest clients" attacks on federated-learning defences;
- classic IDS alert flooding ("squealing", Stick/Snot);
- data poisoning of conformal prediction;
- AHA's full text.
verdict.closest: For the theorem: CAPTURE (arXiv:2609.02265), Theorem 2, a static single-statistic impossibility FUR + RRL >= 1 - delta_phi, together with arXiv:2609.23254, Remark 4, the non-adversarial "no free tuning" safety-vs-recalibration trade-off. The overall foundation is arXiv:2607.21673 (WARDEN/CDC): its Theorem 15 two-world ceiling, the Appendix D.2 dictionary starvation, and its documented CDC tau = +infinity fallback.

hits.title: The Price of Self-Calibration: Exact Evidence Budgets and Manufactured Blind Sets in Adaptive Monitoring (A.-R. Atarmla, arXiv:2609.23254, cs.LG, submitted 19 Sep 2026)
hits.how_close: CLOSEST on theory, but it does not kill the idea. It formalises the absorb horn without any adversary. Theorem 4 and Corollary 2 say a monitor with uniform size over a tolerated drift class D cannot see any fault in D-D, and for speed-bounded drift that blind set is exactly the 2v class. Corollary 3 adds that a certification regime treating absorbed drift as normal 'manufactures' that blind set. Remark 4 ('no free tuning') is a NON-ADVERSARIAL version of the two horns for one gain parameter: slower adaptation narrows the blind set only at the price of 'longer miscalibration after legitimate changes', and 'no setting removes both costs'. Missing from the paper (checked in the HTML): no attacker model (it says adversarial exploitation is 'possible but not required'), no deliberate tripping of a refusal, no trip cost c(tau), no analysis of the period after an attacker leaves, no safety/liveness contract, no rollback, gating or freezing, no IDS or IoT. The proposed theorem must be framed as the adversarial, any-gate generalisation of Remark 4 and must cite it, or reviewers will call it a corollary of this paper.

hits.title: Self-Poisoning in Adaptive Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Sharp-Threshold Theory and Certified Label-Free Calibration (V. B. Balachandran, arXiv:2607.21673, submitted 23 Jul 2026)
hits.how_close: VERY CLOSE: this is the source of WARDEN, CDC and the Theorem 15 the idea builds on. Confirmed from the HTML: WARDEN is a certified admission gate that reads only a frozen reserve. CDC ('certified decontaminated calibration') sets tau = F_mix^-1(1 - alpha(1 - pi_up) + eps_n), where pi_up is an upper bound on a Storey estimate (lambda = 1/2) and eps_n = sqrt(log(2/eta)/(2n)) + 1/n. Theorem 15 ('Two-world indistinguishability') caps power at kappa = alpha/(pi + alpha(1 - pi)). Partial pre-emption of the trip horn: in Appendix D.2, a tail-mimicry attack makes 'the dictionary starve', so decisions fall back to the base channel at alpha/2. The paper calls this a power effect, not a validity effect. Separately it reports that static calibration reaches 1.94x nominal FPR under drift. It never connects the two, never analyses drift during starvation, and never mentions liveness. Not addressed at all: the CDC blinding attack. The paper treats upward bias in pi_up as the conservative direction, and never covers the case where the level 1 - alpha(1 - pi_up) + eps_n reaches or exceeds 1 (Appendix B.3 only gives the level interval). Its limitations say only a tail-mimicry attack was tested. Evaluation is on vision, text and document data; no IDS or IoT.

hits.title: Adversarial concept drift detection under poisoning attacks for robust data stream mining (L. Korycki, B. Krawczyk), Machine Learning (Springer), online 2 Jun 2022, DOI 10.1007/s10994-022-06177-w; arXiv:2009.09497 (2020)
hits.how_close: CLOSE conceptual precursor to both horns. Its 'concept-based poisoning' can (a) inject fake drift during stable periods, causing false alarms and costly adaptations and wasting the labelling budget, or (b) inject adversarial concepts that 'reinforce the old concept', masking real drift and causing a 'lack of adaptation'. Its defence is the robust RBM drift detector RRBM-DD. The name 'CB-RBM' does not appear on the arXiv page or in the part of the PMC text I read. Differences: (b) works by hiding drift from the detector, not by deliberately tripping a refusal gate. There is no impossibility theorem, no safety/liveness contract, and no analysis after the attacker leaves (it only mentions 'increased recovery times'). It is a desktop stream classifier, not IoT IDS.

hits.title: Adversarially Robust Change Point Detection (M. Li, Y. Yu), NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2105.10417
hits.how_close: MODERATE, a theory foundation. Under Huber eps-contamination, an adversary can 'create spurious change points or disguise true change points' (both directions). It shows a phase transition in the detection boundary and gives the minimax-optimal ARC method. It is offline, univariate mean change-point detection: no adaptive self-learner, no gate, no liveness. It should be cited as prior two-sided contamination theory.

hits.title: The Boiling Frog Threshold: Criticality and Blindness in World Model-Based Anomaly Detection Under Gradual Drift (Zhe Hong, arXiv:2603.08455, 9 Mar 2026)
hits.how_close: LOW to MODERATE: the absorb horn only, and not adversarial. Drift below a sharp threshold is absorbed as normal (z-score, variance and percentile detectors); sinusoidal drift is undetectable. Domain is MuJoCo RL. No freeze or trip horn, no IDS.

hits.title: Adversarial Attacks for Drift Detection (F. Hinder, V. Vaquet, B. Hammer), ESANN 2025, pp. 555ff
hits.how_close: LOW to MODERATE: absorb side only. It builds 'drift adversarials', streams whose drift goes undetected, through metric and window adversarials, with necessary and sufficient conditions. The text separates false-positive from false-negative attacks but builds only the false-negative ones. No adaptive defence, no freeze, no liveness.

hits.title: On the Adversarial Risk of Test Time Adaptation: An Investigation into Realistic Test-Time Data Poisoning (Su et al.), ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.04682
hits.how_close: MODERATE for the EATA target. It notes that TePA's high-entropy poison fails EATA's entropy threshold and class-diverse weighting, and designs a Balanced Low-Entropy attack to get past those filters. That is the absorb direction. It does not deliberately trip the filter to starve adaptation and then exploit drift afterwards. The EATA trip attack is therefore not pre-empted, but this is the baseline it must beat.

hits.title: Test-Time Poisoning Attacks Against Test-Time Adaptation Models (T. Cong, X. He, Y. Shen, Y. Zhang), IEEE S&P 2024, arXiv:2308.08505
hits.how_close: LOW to MODERATE: poisoning TTA through its update (10 poisoned samples drop accuracy from 76.20% to 41.83%). Absorb horn only, no gate-tripping.

hits.title: Uncovering Adversarial Risks of Test-Time Adaptation (DIA; Wu et al.), ICML 2023, PMLR v202
hits.how_close: LOW: batch-level malicious samples hijack BN and entropy TTA. This is background for how injected traffic can shift the statistics the gate sees, but it targets misclassifying others' samples, not freezing.

hits.title: R.I.P.: A Simple Black-box Attack on Continual Test-time Adaptation (T.-H. Hoang, D. M. Vo, M. N. Do), arXiv:2412.01154, Dec 2024
hits.how_close: LOW: a black-box attack that reuses incorrect predictions to degrade continual TTA. It does not target reset, rollback or filter mechanisms.

hits.title: When and Where to Reset Matters for Long-Term Test-Time Adaptation (T. Lim, J.-W. Hwang, K. Lee), ICLR 2026, arXiv:2603.03796
hits.how_close: LOW: an adaptive reset triggered by prediction bias, which is a gate that rolls back. It has no adversarial analysis. An attack that forces repeated resets (the analogue of the T2T rollback attack) was not found.

hits.title: Short Paper: Empirical Analysis of Evasion and Poisoning Against Malware Data Drift Detection (M. Yang, D. Lie, N. Papernot, U. Toronto/Vector), workshop short paper (file name says SecAI 2026; venue not confirmed)
hits.how_close: LOW to MODERATE for the DriftXpert labelling-queue idea. It attacks CADE and Transcendent drift detectors, where the victim manually inspects only the top-k drifted samples. The attacks evade the top-k or clean-label poison the retraining set. It does not flood the queue to freeze adaptation and does not discuss liveness.

hits.title: Candidate Comparability Before Promotion: Conditional Validation in Adaptive Network Intrusion Detection (Fernandez-Barrios et al., arXiv:2609.04388, 3 Sep 2026)
hits.how_close: LOW: drift-alarm-triggered retraining and promotion in adaptive NIDS (CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15, ToN-IoT). A search snippet says an adversary steering alarms or challengers is acknowledged but scoped out; the abstract I fetched covers no adversary.

hits.title: ACORN-IDS: Adaptive Continual Novelty Detection for Intrusion Detection Systems (S. Fuhrman, O. Gungor, T. Rosing), arXiv:2602.07291, Feb 2026
hits.how_close: TARGET, not prior attack work. Confirmed: the threshold is mu + 2*sigma of PCA reconstruction error, recomputed after every task (Algorithm 1). No poisoning or adversarial analysis, so the threshold-inflation attack on it is unclaimed.

hits.title: When Normality Shifts: Risk-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for Unsupervised Tabular Anomaly Detection (RTTAD), arXiv:2605.10242, May 2026
hits.how_close: TARGET. It selectively updates on high-confidence pseudo-normal samples, with a gamma-GMM confidence threshold. It is tabular, not network traffic. The abstract mentions no stop rule and no adversary, so I could NOT verify the 'stop rule' the idea plans to trigger.

hits.title: Anomaly Detection in the Open World: Normality Shift Detection, Explanation, and Adaptation (OWAD), NDSS 2023
hits.how_close: TARGET. No attack papers on OWAD's shift detection or adaptation were found.

hits.title: ANTIDOTE: Understanding and Defending against Poisoning of Anomaly Detectors (Rubinstein et al.), ACM IMC 2009
hits.how_close: BACKGROUND for the absorb and boiling-frog horn. Its detector's threshold is computed from the poisoned traffic, so inflating a threshold through training statistics is old in general. That reduces the novelty of mean + k*SD inflation as a mechanism, but not of applying it to modern defences.

hits.title: Security Analysis of Online Centroid Anomaly Detection (Kloft, Laskov), JMLR 2012
hits.how_close: BACKGROUND: how far the attacker can displace an online centroid detector depends on traffic share. Absorb horn only.

hits.title: Can't Boil This Frog: Robustness of Online-Trained Autoencoder-Based Anomaly Detectors to Adversarial Poisoning Attacks, arXiv:2002.02741
hits.how_close: BACKGROUND: boiling-frog poisoning of online autoencoders through the drift-update mechanism. Absorb horn only.

hits.title: Demonstrating and Characterizing Frog-Boiling Poisoning Against Drift-Aware Continual Learners (UMass Dartmouth thesis defence announcement, 11 Aug 2026, advisor G. Kul)
hits.how_close: LOW to MODERATE: a white-box boiling-frog attack on an SSF-adaptive IDS autoencoder. Absorb horn only. Only the event page exists; no paper could be verified.

hits.title: Robust Conformal Intrusion Detection via Traffic-Aware Calibration and Attack-Orbit Invariance, arXiv:2609.19241 (Sep 2026)
hits.how_close: LOW: conformal IDS calibration under feature-perturbation evasion. It does not inflate the calibrator or blind it through contamination estimates, and covers no adaptive or self-learning detector.

hits.title: Defending Against Adversarial Denial-of-Service Data Poisoning Attacks, arXiv:2104.06744 (ACM DL 10.1145/3477997.3478017; venue not verified)
hits.how_close: LOW: availability (denial-of-service) poisoning, where the goal is to make the model unusable. It is a distant relative of the liveness horn and involves no gate.

hits.conclusion:
I could not find prior work that already does this idea. The novelty sits in a narrower place than the pitch suggests, because two very recent preprints cover most of the theory.

Search coverage is incomplete. The shared web-search limit (200 searches per turn) ran out partway through. I verified the remaining papers only by fetching their pages directly. These searches did not run: FL 'framing' attacks (making honest clients look malicious), IDS alarm-flooding precedents, plasticity-loss attacks, and searches for the unverified defence names. Send a follow-up message to continue them.

(1) What is already covered:
- **The absorb (boiling-frog) horn** is old: ANTIDOTE 2009, Kloft & Laskov 2012, Can't Boil This Frog 2020. Two 2026 preprints formalise it:
  - arXiv:2609.23254 proves the D-D blind set, which is exactly the 2v class for speed-bounded drift.
  - arXiv:2607.21673 (the WARDEN/CDC paper) gives the Theorem 15 two-world indistinguishability ceiling.
- **A non-adversarial version of the two horns exists.** Remark 4 of 2609.23254 says that slowing adaptation narrows the blind set only by lengthening miscalibration after legitimate changes, and that no setting removes both costs. The 'both horns' theorem must be positioned as the adversarial, any-gate generalisation of that remark. It must be more than a restatement: an explicit trip cost c(tau), post-departure FPR of about 1 - Phi(z_alpha - v*tau/s), and a liveness clause covering L cycles after the attacker leaves. Otherwise it reads as a corollary of 2609.23254 plus WARDEN Theorem 15.
- **WARDEN's own Appendix D.2 already shows the trip horn empirically.** Tail-mimicry makes the dictionary starve and fall back to the base channel. The same paper separately shows static calibration reaching 1.94x nominal FPR under drift. It never joins the two, never examines drift during starvation, and never mentions liveness.
- **Korycki & Krawczyk** (Machine Learning, 2022) already describe two attacker goals: fake drift that forces costly adaptation and wastes the labelling budget, and 'lack of adaptation' by reinforcing the old concept. Their mechanism is masking drift from the detector, not tripping a refusal, and they have no theorem or contract.
- **Li & Yu** (NeurIPS 2021) show contamination can create or hide change points, but only offline and with no adaptive learner.
- **Threshold inflation of mean + k*SD** is generically old (ANTIDOTE).

(2) What I could not find anywhere:
- Adversarial gate-tripping, or freezing, used as an attack that pays off after the attacker leaves.
- A safety-plus-liveness contract for self-learning detectors.
- An impossibility result for all single-stream suspicion gates g(S_t).
- A corollary that a refusal region honest drift cannot reach (directional, TOA-style) escapes both horns.
- Blinding CDC by inflating Storey's pi_up until the level 1 - alpha(1 - pi_up) + eps_n is at or above 1. The source paper treats upward pi_up bias as conservative and never covers that case.
- 'Ring inflation' against a signature-free core/ring method.
- Attacks on OWAD, ACORN-IDS (threshold verified as mu + 2*sigma, refreshed per task), RTTAD, or EATA-style filters in starvation mode. Su et al. (ICLR 2025) bypass EATA's filter; nobody trips it.
- Attacks that force repeated resets in TTA. The ICLR 2026 reset paper has no adversary.

(3) Verification problems in the idea text:
- I could not confirm that 'T2T rollback', 'DriftXpert' (OR > T trigger), 'LID box' or 'RPS' are published. Searches for T2T and DriftXpert returned nothing, and no search I ran surfaced LID box or RPS. Get exact citations before claiming 'six published defences'.
- I could not confirm RTTAD's stop rule from its abstract, and RTTAD is a tabular method, not a network-traffic one.
- 'CB-RBM' does not appear on the Korycki & Krawczyk arXiv page or in the part of the PMC text I read; their detector is called RRBM-DD.
- Every 2026 hit is an arXiv preprint, not peer-reviewed.

Verdict: the idea survives. It must cite 2609.23254 (Remark 4, Corollary 3) and 2607.21673 (Theorem 15, Appendix D.2 starvation) as the closest work. It is strongest framed as: (a) the first adversarial trip/freeze attack with a liveness contract and a cost-of-trip bound; (b) the CDC blinding attack; (c) the directional-refusal corollary.

hits.title: Self-Poisoning in Adaptive Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Sharp-Threshold Theory and Certified Label-Free Calibration (WARDEN + CDC), V. B. Balachandran
hits.how_close: CLOSEST, and it already covers the core of the safety horn. Theorem 15 (Sec. 6) builds the two-world construction on the 1-D score: World A is benign drift P'=(1-pi)P+pi*Q, World B is tail contamination. It proves {FPR_A<=alpha} is a subset of {TPR_B<=kappa}, with kappa=alpha/(pi+alpha(1-pi)). So 'no label-free rule both tracks drift and catches tail-mimicking poison' is already published. Two other points also overlap your dual. (1) CDC sets tau=+infinity ('flag nothing', trivially valid) when the requested quantile goes above 1. (2) Corollary 10 says an adversary can 'suppress the dictionary channel's contribution to decisions', which it calls 'a power effect rather than a validity effect'. So blinding CDC exploits a degenerate case the paper itself documents. What it does NOT cover: an attacker who deliberately trips the gate to stall admissions (freeze/liveness), post-departure FPR, a safety-plus-liveness contract, an analysis of the cost of inflating Storey's pi_up, or any attack on IoT/NIDS defences. Its Limitations section says only the tail-mimicry attack was stress-tested. Your 'both horns' theorem has to be presented as a strict extension (an active freeze horn) and not as new indistinguishability.

hits.title: Adversarial concept drift detection under poisoning attacks for robust data stream mining, Ł. Korycki & B. Krawczyk, Machine Learning (Springer)
hits.how_close: Close at the level of concepts, so you must cite it and draw the distinction. Its taxonomy already names three attacker goals against adaptive learners. (1) 'Forcing false and unnecessary adaptation' (false drift alarms). (2) 'Impairing the adaptation process', where poison can 'significantly slow down the adaptation process'. (3) A 'lack of adaptation' case, where adversarial concepts that reinforce the old concept 'mask the appearance of the real concept drift and inhibit any drift detection or adaptation mechanisms'. That is a freeze-type goal. However, the mechanism differs: it masks drift by reinforcing the old concept, rather than tripping a suspicion or refusal gate. There is no theorem, no safety/liveness contract, no post-departure FPR analysis and no NIDS evaluation. Their defence is a robust RBM drift detector (RRBM-DD).

hits.title: Robust Conformal Outlier Detection under Contaminated Reference Data, M. Bashari, M. Sesia, Y. Romano (ICML 2025)
hits.how_close: Close to the blinding horn. It proves that calibrating on contaminated reference data makes conformal outlier detection conservative: type-I error stays controlled but power drops, because outliers push the calibration scores up. This is the same mechanism as inflating a label-free threshold. It is explicitly non-adversarial: the authors set aside worst-case adversarial contamination. Their fix (Label-Trim) uses a small labelling budget. Not an attack paper, and it does not cover Storey pi_up, gates or freezing. Expect reviewers to say 'contamination causes loss of power is known', so the novelty you claim has to be how cheaply an attacker gets there and the direction-weighted budget fix.

hits.title: Adversarial Attacks for Drift Detection ('drift adversarials'), F. Hinder, V. Vaquet, B. Hammer (ESANN 2025)
hits.how_close: Moderate. It constructs streams that drift without being detected and computes all such adversarials for common detection schemes. This is a boiling-frog/safety-horn result against drift detectors in general. It does not consider attacks that force alarms or freezes, adaptive defences, gates, liveness, or security data (full-text grep: no retraining/poisoning analysis).

hits.title: Security Analysis of Online Centroid Anomaly Detection, M. Kloft & P. Laskov (JMLR 13)
hits.how_close: Foundation for both 'minimum time to compromise' (bounds on poisoning a centroid when the attacker's share is bounded) and ring/radius inflation. The paper notes that learning the radius 'would open the system to poisoning attacks against the radius' and leaves the radius fixed. This anticipates your ring-inflation dual against your own signature-free method. No freeze or liveness analysis.

hits.title: Allergy Attack Against Automatic Signature Generation, S. P. Chung & A. K. Mok (RAID 2006, Springer LNCS)
hits.how_close: Historical precedent for turning a self-learning defence into a false-positive/DoS generator ('an active agent for DoS attack against the protected system'). The mechanism differs: it makes the learner learn benign traffic as malicious, rather than freezing a gated learner while honest drift accumulates. I could see only the abstract and metadata, not the full text.

hits.title: Continuous Learning for Android Malware Detection, Y. Chen, Z. Ding, D. Wagner (USENIX Security 2023)
hits.how_close: Partial overlap with your DriftXpert labelling-queue attack. It describes an attacker who crafts samples the active-learning selector will pick for human labelling (clean-label poisoning through the selector) and calls defending active learning against this 'an open problem'. Integrity horn only. It does not cover flooding the queue to exhaust the budget or freezing adaptation.

hits.title: Compromising PCA-based Anomaly Detectors for Network-Wide Traffic (boiling-frog poisoning), Rubinstein et al., UC Berkeley EECS-2008-73 (precursor of ANTIDOTE, IMC 2009)
hits.how_close: Origin of the boiling-frog poisoning horn on network anomaly detectors (gradual week-over-week poisoning). No gate-tripping or freeze.

hits.title: Can't Boil This Frog: Robustness of Online-Trained Autoencoder-Based Anomaly Detectors to Adversarial Poisoning Attacks, M. Kravchik & A. Shabtai
hits.how_close: Safety horn only: gradual poisoning of retrained ICS autoencoders, which works only for limited attack types. No freeze, liveness or gating analysis.

hits.title: Robust Anomaly based Attack Detection in Smart Grids under Data Poisoning Attacks, Bhattacharjee et al. (ACM CPSS 2022)
hits.how_close: Close to your threshold-inflation dual for mean+k*SD and percentile refreshes. It poisons the threshold-learning step (white-box FGAV and black-box RSL) so that attacks fall below the learned threshold. Not framed as blinding a label-free calibrator, and no freeze horn. Seen only through search snippets.

hits.title: On the Adversarial Risk of Test Time Adaptation: An Investigation into Realistic Test-Time Data Poisoning
hits.how_close: Relevant to your EATA target. Per search snippets, it reports that entropy-maximising poison is 'easily defended' by entropy thresholding, and so it designs low-entropy and class-balanced (BLE) attacks to get past EATA/ROID filters. Integrity horn only. It treats high-entropy samples being filtered out as a failed attack and never reframes it as freezing adaptation.
