hits.how_close: Shows that entropy filters (ETA, SoTTA) fail because malicious samples are crafted to be low-entropy, and that EMA defences carry a robustness-vs-adaptation trade-off. It names the trade-off informally but has no attacker that exploits the robust side (freeze) and no theorem.

hits.title: Uncovering Adversarial Risks of Test-Time Adaptation (DIA), Wu et al. (ICML 2023)
hits.how_close: Founding TTA poisoning attack: malicious samples in a batch corrupt predictions on benign samples. Integrity horn only.

hits.title: On the Adversarial Vulnerability of Label-Free Test-Time Adaptation, Rifat et al. (ICLR 2025)
hits.how_close: Label-free attack on TTA that raises error; finds that existing defences are 'almost ineffective'. Integrity horn only. It does not cover freezing, resets or liveness.

hits.title: R.I.P.: A Simple Black-box Attack on Continual Test-time Adaptation, Hoang, Vo, Do
hits.how_close: Black-box attack that degrades continual TTA over time by re-feeding misclassified samples. Integrity/collapse horn only; it does not exploit reset or filter mechanisms.

hits.title: When and Where to Reset Matters for Long-Term Test-Time Adaptation (ASR)
hits.how_close: A reset/rollback-style defence triggered by a statistic of the model's own predictions. This is the same structure as your T2T rollback target, but the paper never considers an adversary firing the reset. It is a potential extra target, not prior work on the attack.

hits.title: Learn to Adapt: Robust Drift Detection in Security Domain, A. Kuppa & N.-A. Le-Khac
hits.how_close: Says periodic retraining is 'not robust towards attacker-induced drifts' and claims robustness to adversarial drift. It does not analyse an attacker manipulating the detector to force or suppress retraining.

hits.title: Navigating the Latent Manifold: Proactive Concept Drift Adaptation for Resilient NIDS (DriftXpert)
hits.how_close: Your TARGET, confirmed real. It uses label-free clustering drift indicators CI and OR, plus selective freezing and weight aggregation. The abstract has no adversarial analysis. Caveat on your 'public code' plan: a GitHub issue (https://github.com/cc-sec-hub/DriftXpert/issues/1) says the released code is incomplete, especially the Phase-2 adaptation.

hits.how_close: Your TARGET, confirmed. It updates only on high-confidence pseudo-normal samples (TTCL) and has no adversarial analysis. hits.title: Mateen: Adaptive Ensemble Learning for Network Anomaly Detection, Alotaibi & Maffeis (RAID 2024)
hits.how_close: Not an attack paper. It is an extra candidate target: an online shift-detection and adaptation NIDS that labels only 1% of samples. It mentions poisoning only as future work (full-text grep).

hits.title: The Boiling Frog Threshold: Criticality and Blindness in World Model-Based Anomaly Detection Under Gradual Drift, Z. Hong
hits.how_close: Low. Non-adversarial: a sharp drift-absorption threshold epsilon* for z-score, variance and percentile detectors in RL agents. No attacker and no safety/liveness trade-off.

hits.title: Can Drift-Adaptive Malware Detectors Be Made Robust? Attacks and Defenses Under White-Box and Black-Box Threats
hits.how_close: Low. Evasion (PGD, MalGuise) against the drift-adaptive AdvDA. Nothing on gating, freezing or calibration.

hits.title: A Framework for Drift Detection and Adaptation in AI-driven Anomaly and Threat Detection Systems (HDDAF), Lara-Gutierrez et al., Int. J. Inf. Security 24
hits.how_close: Low. A hybrid drift-adaptation IDS framework. No attack on retraining triggers (full-text grep).

hits.title: Adapting Under Fire: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Adversarial Drift in Network Security (SECRYPT 2025)
hits.how_close: Low. The red agent's goal is evasion, and nothing in it disrupts the defender's adaptation.

hits.conclusion:
I could not kill the idea outright. No paper I found formalises the gate-tripping (freeze) attack on a suspicion-gated self-learner, the safety-plus-liveness contract, or the 'both horns' impossibility. No paper attacks any of the named NIDS defences either. But large parts of the idea are already published, and the paper has to be scoped around them.

What is already published:
(1) The two-world indistinguishability core is WARDEN's Theorem 15 (arXiv 2607.21673, Jul 2026). It already shows that FPR control under benign drift caps power under tail contamination at kappa. So the safety horn is close to a restatement; the freeze horn is the real addition.
(2) Korycki & Krawczyk (Machine Learning 2022) already name 'lack of adaptation / masking real drift', 'impairing adaptation' and 'forcing false adaptation' as attacker goals. They get there by a different mechanism (reinforcing the old concept), not by tripping a refusal gate, and they give no theorem. You must cite them and draw the distinction.
(3) The blinding dual is weakly novel. WARDEN itself documents CDC's tau=+infinity fallback and says in Corollary 10 that an adversary can cause 'a power effect rather than a validity effect'. Bashari, Sesia & Romano (ICML 2025) prove that contaminated calibration makes conformal outlier detection conservative and costs power, though in a non-adversarial setting. Kloft & Laskov (JMLR 2012) already warned that a learned radius invites poisoning of the radius. Bhattacharjee et al. (CPSS 2022) poison threshold learning. What is still new: the attacker's cost to reach blinding, the direction-weighted radius budget, and a minimum time to blind.
(4) The TTA attack papers (DIA, MedBN, 2410.04682, Rifat et al. ICLR 2025, RIP) are all on the integrity horn. 2410.04682 even treats 'high-entropy poison gets filtered by EATA' as a failed attack, which is the gap your freeze framing fills.

Practical warnings from verification:
- I could not locate T2T (the rollback rule at 2.5x the mean of the last 5 scores), the LID box defence, or CB-RBM, so I cannot confirm these papers or their rules.
- I could not confirm RTTAD's stop rule from its abstract.
- ACORN-IDS computes mu+2*sigma on a trusted clean validation split, so inflating it needs attacker access to that split.
- DriftXpert's public code is reportedly incomplete (GitHub issue #1).
- Per-sample filters (EATA, RTTAD) may fall outside your single-stream-gate model. Freezing them requires honest drift itself to reach the refusal region, which your corollary should state explicitly.
- WARDEN is a single-author preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

I hit the 200-search session limit before I could search adversarial quickest-change-detection (CUSUM false-alarm or delay attacks), 'framing honest clients' attacks on detection-based FL defences, EATA itself, and the Paragraph/red-herring attacks. Those are the remaining places a direct kill could be hiding. A follow-up message can resume the search there.

hits.title: Self-Poisoning in Adaptive Out-of-Distribution Detection: A Sharp-Threshold Theory and Certified Label-Free Calibration (WARDEN gate + CDC; V. B. Balachandran)
hits.how_close: CLOSEST, and it partly pre-empts the blinding dual. This is the source of the idea's Theorem 15 (two-world: drift and contamination give identical unlabelled stream laws, so TPR <= kappa = alpha/(pi+alpha(1-pi))). The full text already says that when the CDC level goes above 1 it sets tau=+inf and flags nothing, which it calls 'trivially valid', i.e. a power loss and not a validity failure. Its Corollary 10 says an adversary can 'suppress the dictionary channel' (again a power effect). Under its mimicry attack, App. D.2 shows 'the dictionary starves' and TPR falls from 0.615 to 0.004 ('What the adversary does achieve is hiding'), while 'Realized FPR never rises under attack'. It does NOT model Storey pi_up inflation by benign-looking off points, a time-to-blind, gate-tripping/freezing, or any liveness / post-departure FPR property. Sec. 8 says its adversarial testing is narrow (mimicry only). So the blinding horn must be framed as an active, cost-bounded construction with a time-to-blind, not as 'CDC can be blinded', because WARDEN already concedes that as a power loss.

hits.title: CAPTURE: Disentangling Preference Drift from Memory Poisoning in Personalized LLM Agents (Hossain, Shayoni, Morol)
hits.how_close: VERY CLOSE in the form of its theorem, different domain. Appendix A.3, Theorem 2 ('Impossibility'): FUR(d) + RRL(d) >= 1 - delta_phi for any rule that reads only the statistic phi. FUR is the rate of accepting injected claims and RRL the rate of rejecting genuine revisions. That is a static Le Cam two-point version of 'a single-statistic gate either accepts poison or refuses honest drift'. It also argues that a history-conditioned rule is never worse, which echoes the idea's corollary. It reports an 'adaptation-security tradeoff' empirically. BUT: the setting is LLM agent memory, not IDS. RRL is a passive defender error; no attacker deliberately drives RRL up (no freeze attack, no trip cost c(tau), no post-departure FPR / liveness). The 'both horns' theorem must cite this and claim only its dynamic, attacker-triggered liveness part as new.

hits.title: Theory of Continual Learning Against Data Poisoning Attacks (Hu, Duan) - source of the T2T defence
hits.how_close: CLOSE, partial pre-emption of the freeze cost. This is the T2T target. Verified: Alg. 1 rolls back to w_t = w_{t-2}. App. E.1 flags a task when the score is more than 2.5x the mean of the previous five scores. It proves that no defence succeeds when the adversary poisons a linear fraction of tasks (a poisoning-only impossibility). Sec. 5 notes that under pervasive poisoning 'a rejection-based strategy' discards the whole sequence, a 'total loss of system utility'. It never considers an attacker who spikes the score on purpose to force repeated rollbacks, and never quantifies false triggers under benign shift (the 'attribution dilemma' is raised but not analysed). The T2T trip attack is still open; the utility-loss remark should be cited.

hits.title: Adversarial Concept Drift Detection under Poisoning Attacks for Robust Data Stream Mining (Korycki, Krawczyk)
hits.year: arXiv 2020; Machine Learning journal 2023 (Springer DOI 10.1007/s10994-022-06177-w; journal page not fetched)
hits.how_close: MODERATE, BACKGROUND. In prose it lists attacker goals that anticipate both horns and the DriftXpert queue flood: (i) 'Forcing false and unnecessary adaptation'; (ii) 'Impairing the adaptation process', up to 'complete nullification' and slowing adaptation to real drift; (iii) 'Hindering label query process', where fake-novel points use up the labelling budget. Its remedy is a trainable RBM drift detector. There is no gate model, no safety/liveness contract, no theorem, and no attack on gated defences. It kills any claim that 'attacks that impair adaptation' or 'label-queue flooding' are new ideas. It does not kill the formal two-horn result or the per-defence trip attacks.

hits.title: Security Analysis of Online Centroid Anomaly Detection (Kloft, Laskov)
hits.year: 2010 (arXiv; a JMLR 2012 version exists but was not verified here)
hits.how_close: FOUNDATION (background). It proposes exactly a suspicion gate g: watch the false-positive rate and, when a threshold is exceeded, load a safe state and switch off online updates (Sec. 6.1, 7.7). If the threshold is crossed, the attack is counted as 'failed'. It explicitly puts 'red herring' availability attacks (junk that causes false alarms) out of scope. So it never considers an attacker tripping the switch-off on purpose to freeze learning under drift. Useful as the classic gate the freeze horn applies to, and as evidence that the gap is long-standing.

hits.title: Adversarial Attacks for Drift Detection (Hinder, Vaquet, Hammer)
