hits.year: 2023 v1 / 2024 v2 (DOI 10.1145/3644815.3644961; venue appears to be CAIN 2024, not verified)
hits.how_close: Weak. It compares 'blind' scheduled retraining with retraining triggered by a drift detector. It does not use external change events and has no security model. Cite it only for the scheduled-versus-drift-triggered framing.

hits.title: Continual Learning with Strategic Selection and Forgetting for Network Intrusion Detection (Zhang et al.), IEEE INFOCOM 2025
hits.how_close: Weak. It adapts a NIDS to drift continually through a selected or forgotten memory buffer. There are no authenticated triggers and the abstract does not discuss poisoning. It is a good example of an always-learning detector your bound could be applied to.

hits.title: Security Analysis of Online Centroid Anomaly Detection (Kloft, Laskov), JMLR 13:3681-3724
hits.how_close: Foundation for your bound, not for the event mechanism. It bounds the poisoning attacker's gain against an online centroid detector. Without constraints the attacker succeeds; with external constraints (limited control, bounded false-positive rate) there is a strict upper bound. Your B*t + N_lic*K*B_L*kappa_rev bound is in this tradition and must cite it.

hits.title: Adversarial Concept Drift Detection under Poisoning Attacks for Robust Data Stream Mining (Korycki, Krawczyk)
hits.how_close: Adjacent. It separates real drift from adversarial drift with a trainable detector based on a Restricted Boltzmann Machine. This is the 'infer whether drift is benign' approach your idea replaces with cryptographic attestation of benign-drift events.

hits.title: Poisoning Attacks on Cyber Attack Detectors for Industrial Control Systems (Kravchik, Biggio, Shabtai), arXiv:2012.15740
hits.how_close: Threat-model foundation: periodic online retraining that admits only non-alerting data still lets slow poisoning succeed. This motivates a small background budget B. It has no event gating.

hits.title: The Frog-Boiling Attack: Limitations of Anomaly Detection for Secure Network Coordinate Systems (Chan-Tin, Feldman, Hopper, Kim)
hits.how_close: Origin of the slow-drift (boiling-frog) attack your background budget is meant to bound. It has no defense of the event-licence type.

hits.conclusion:
VERDICT: The idea is not killed, but it is wounded. Its headline mechanism, 'an external event temporarily raises the anomaly detector's learning rate', is already prior art in Cisco patent US9923911B2 (priority 2015, granted 2018). There, an NMS-originated NEW-APP message makes the learning agent enter a 'fast learning mode' and 'increase its learning rate temporarily'. The agent keeps the old model in parallel and can suppress alerts in an 'observation mode'. Claim 10 explicitly recites increasing the training rate. The firmware-update version of the problem also has older solutions: DÏoT (ICDCS 2019) cancels alarms and triggers re-learning when fleet-wide alarms correlate, with a human confirming; Sivanathan's thesis has an operator confirm the upgrade, then retrains. ICS practice (MITRE-aligned guidance from vendor and practitioner sources, not peer-reviewed) already advises gating retraining on approved change tickets and maintenance windows. The MUD acceptable-URLs IETF draft (2024) already gives the gateway a signer-pinned, firmware-update-driven signal, but uses it for ACL policy, not learning. You must cite all of these and must not claim 'event-triggered fast adaptation' as new.

WHAT I FOUND NO PRIOR ART FOR (the defensible novelty):
(1) Making the trigger a cryptographically signed, scoped, time-boxed token. It would bind device_id, event_type, fw_hash or config_hash, t_start, K and scope, be verified at the gateway, and come from the OTA path only after image verification. Cisco's message is unauthenticated, DÏoT's trigger is statistical plus human, and MUD's signal is not used for learning.
(2) A two-rate (B, B_L) budget with a formal displacement bound, B*t + N_lic*K*B_L*kappa_rev, where N_lic cannot be raised without the signing key. Kloft and Laskov (JMLR 2012) is the closest bound-style foundation, but it has no event licensing.
(3) A directional revert of only the threat-subspace component of the licence-period change, as an alternative to full rollback, freezing or suppression. Cisco only keeps the old model in parallel. The Cisco cold-start patent suspends learning on suspicion, which is the behaviour your idea rejects.
(4) Spawning instances only on a provisioning licence, with the new instance initialised from a peer prior. This directly answers Ino et al. (Sensors 24(19):6416, 2024). That paper confirms the attack (the drift detector auto-spawns a poisoned instance) and explicitly leaves countermeasures to future work.

RISKS TO STATE IN THE PAPER: an attacker can time poisoning to coincide with legitimate licence windows, so kappa_rev and the quality of the threat subspace U carry the whole bound. A legitimately signed but malicious update (supply-chain attack, or a stolen key) gets B_L for free. A compromised device could replay or withhold tokens, which t_start, a nonce or counter, and gateway-side verification must address. The paper should compare against an inferred-event baseline (traffic-based firmware-change detection, Andrews et al., ACM TOIT 2026) and a DÏoT-style correlation baseline.

LIMITS OF THIS SEARCH: The session's web-search budget ran out partway through. I could not search ESP32/TinyML on-device-learning defenses, cold-start or peer-prior onboarding for new devices, SUIT-manifest-plus-IDS work, or certified or rate-limited continual NIDS. You can send a follow-up message to continue the search on those, or raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION. I could not open the Columbia Academic Commons report on updating anomaly-sensor models after patching (access denied), so it is unverified and not listed. I did not open the CCS'25 'Adversarial Habituation Attack' poster (403) or the UMass Dartmouth frog-boiling talk (404), so their contents are unverified; both are attacks on drift-adaptive detectors and do not appear to propose event licensing. HADES-IoT's firmware re-profiling discussion and the details of Sivanathan's firmware-upgrade handling come from search snippets of their PDFs; I did not read the full texts myself.

hits.title: Anomaly Detection Supporting New Application Deployments (US Patent 9,923,911 B2; Cisco; Vasseur, Dasgupta, Mermoud)
hits.year: 2018 (granted Mar 20 2018; filed Oct 8 2015). BACKGROUND, but a direct foundation
hits.how_close: CLOSEST. This kills the claim that event-triggered fast learning is new. I read the cover page, the claims and description cols 13-14 directly from the scanned PDF. A supervisory agent forwards a NEW-APP message from the network management system to the detector. The message carries the app ID, the expected traffic changes, a schedule and where the app will be deployed. The detector then enters a 'fast learning mode' and 'increase[s] its learning rate temporarily'. Claim 10: 'increasing a training rate for the merged anomaly detection model'. It can keep the old model running in parallel during fast learning, and it has an 'observation mode' that suppresses alerts (claims 5 and 11). WHAT IT LACKS: in the pages I read, the message is not described as cryptographically signed or verified, and there is no scope or K inside a token. There is no slow learning rate that is always on, no bound on how far an attacker can push the model, no revert toward a threat subspace, and nothing about device firmware or provisioning. Its alert-suppression mode is exactly the blind spot your design avoids.

hits.title: HADES-IoT: A Practical Host-Based Anomaly Detection System for IoT Devices (Extended Version); Breitenbacher, Homoliak, Aung, Tippenhauer, Elovici
hits.year: 2019 (arXiv v1, 3 May 2019; I believe the venue is ACM AsiaCCS 2019 but did not confirm it on the page). BACKGROUND
hits.how_close: VERY CLOSE on 'a signed firmware event unlocks re-learning'. I read sections 4.5.2 and 5.3 and Fig. 7 directly. The owner sends commands to the detector signed with Merkle/Lamport one-time signatures, with a replay counter. The update flow: a signed 'disable' command, then the firmware update, then a signed command to re-profile and then re-enable protection. WHAT IT LACKS: it is a host-based whitelist, not a network detector. It fully disables detection and fully re-profiles, which is the freeze-and-disable weakness you argue against. The command comes from a user, not automatically from verified OTA image checks. There is no rate budget, no bound, no directional revert and no peer prior.

hits.title: DÏoT: A Federated Self-learning Anomaly Detection System for IoT; Nguyen, Marchal, Miettinen, Fereidooni, Asokan, Sadeghi (IEEE ICDCS 2019)
hits.how_close: CLOSE on the problem, different mechanism. Section 'Evolution of IoT Device Behavior' (read directly): firmware updates cause false alarms. If many security gateways raise alarms for the same device type in a short window, the alarm is cancelled and the identification and anomaly models are re-learned. A human expert confirms, so that a malware outbreak is not mistaken for an update rollout. The update is inferred from fleet correlation, not signed. Re-learning is a full relearn with no bound, no time box and no revert. A coordinated worm is exactly the case your signed licence handles better.

hits.title: Data Poisoning Attack against Neural Network-Based On-Device Learning Anomaly Detector by Physical Attacks on Sensors; Ino, Yoshida, Matsutani, Fujino (Sensors 24(19):6416)
hits.how_close: ATTACK, NOT PRIOR DEFENSE. Very likely the 'Sensors 2024 hijack' your idea refers to. Verified via the OpenAlex abstract: the detector combines concept-drift detection with multiple models, and acoustic injection into MEMS accelerometers falsifies the data. The detector then trains on the poisoned data and misses anomalies. It supports your licence-gated spawning rule ('unlicensed drift never spawns an instance') but proposes no event-gated defense.

hits.title: Security Analysis of Online Centroid Anomaly Detection; Kloft, Laskov (JMLR vol. 13; arXiv 1003.0078)
hits.how_close: FOUNDATION for your bound. It derives strict upper bounds on how far a poisoning attacker can push an online centroid detector, when the attacker controls a bounded share of traffic or the false-positive rate is bounded. Your B*t term is the same kind of bound. The added licensed term N_lic*K*B_L*kappa_rev, and making N_lic depend on a signing key, do not appear here. I verified the abstract. A search snippet says it also suggests turning off updates when FPR crosses a threshold; I did not verify that.

hits.title: Can't Boil This Frog: Robustness of Online-Trained Autoencoder-Based Anomaly Detectors to Adversarial Poisoning Attacks; Kravchik, Shabtai
hits.how_close: Threat-model background (gradual 'boiling frog' poisoning of online-trained detectors). It reports that autoencoders on SWaT were largely resilient. No event gating. Useful as a baseline attack for evaluating your always-on budget B.

A neighbouring idea: a cryptographically bound vendor artifact (the MUD profile) defines legitimate behaviour, profile updates are secure, and it is implemented on ESP32-S3/C6. The search summary says a new MUD URL can arrive inside the firmware update payload; I did not confirm that on the abstract page. It changes access-control policy only. There is no learned detector, learning rate or bound.

hits.how_close: LOW-MODERATE. Separates runtime-vs-MUD deviation caused by outdated firmware from deviation caused by compromise. Rule-based; no adaptation licensing. Based on a search snippet; I did not fetch the full text. Authors are from memory, not checked on the page.

hits.how_close: LOW, and a naming collision: its 'budget' is a labelling budget for drift caused by firmware updates, not a learning-rate budget. Details come from search snippets only.

hits.title: Security system for in-vehicle network and method therefor (US Patent 12,192,232)
hits.how_close: LOW-MODERATE analog, UNVERIFIED (search snippet only). The gateway switches IDS mode based on diagnostic-session state. Related patents note that an IDS out of sync with the true state can be exploited, which is the same risk as faking an 'OTA happened' signal. No learning-rate licensing.

hits.conclusion:
PARTLY KILLED. The headline idea, that an external device or deployment event temporarily unlocks fast learning, is not new. Your paper must not claim it is.

1. The Cisco patent US 9,923,911 B2 (filed 2015, granted 2018) explicitly describes the detector entering a 'fast learning mode' that 'increase[s] its learning rate temporarily'. It is triggered by a planned-deployment message carrying a schedule and scope, can keep the old model running in parallel, and has an alert-suppressing observation mode. Claim 10 claims increasing the training rate.
2. HADES-IoT (2019) uses signed Merkle/Lamport commands with a replay counter to disable the detector, re-profile it after a firmware update, and re-enable it. That is 'a signed firmware event unlocks re-learning' in host-based form.
3. DÏoT (ICDCS 2019) re-learns after firmware updates when many gateways alarm on the same device type, with human confirmation.

WHAT SURVIVES. I found no 2024-2026 paper (nor older) that combines these four:
(a) A licence token cryptographically bound to the gateway's own check of the OTA image or provisioning, carrying scope and K.
(b) A two-rate design that never freezes, with an explicit bound on attacker displacement, B*t + N_lic*K*B_L*kappa_rev. It extends Kloft and Laskov (JMLR 2012) with a licensed term that depends on the signing key.
(c) A revert at licence end that undoes only the move toward the threat subspace, instead of a full rollback.
(d) Spawning a new per-device instance only under a licence, as a defense against the drift-triggered new-model poisoning of Ino et al. (Sensors 2024).

So reposition the contribution as the bound, the directional revert and the spawn gate. Cite the Cisco patent, HADES-IoT and DÏoT as the event-triggered baselines, and compare against them experimentally:
- Cisco-style unsigned fast-learning mode
- HADES-style disable and re-profile
- DÏoT-style fleet-correlated relearning

OPEN RISKS:
- Signed-but-malicious or downgrade updates (Symmetry 2025) can mint valid licences, so the token needs anti-rollback and monotonic versions.
- kappa_rev < 1 only holds along the known threat subspace U. Displacement toward unknown attacks during a licence is not bounded.
- An attacker who times injections to legitimate licence windows gets the full K*B_L per event.

CAVEATS: The web-search budget ran out partway through. I could not run planned searches for 'selective/directional rollback of poisoned updates', 'ESP32 Secure Boot TinyML IDS with signed OTA', or a further sweep for 2025-2026 OTA-aware IDS, so a closer 2025-2026 paper may still exist. Unverified items:
- Whether the Cisco patent authenticates its message (I read only the cover, the claims and description cols 13-14).
- The HADES-IoT venue.
- The 2026 frog-boiling-vs-SSF thesis.
- The automotive patent details.

hits.title: Microsoft Defender for IoT documentation: 'Create a learned baseline of OT traffic' (with companion page 'Maintain Defender for IoT OT network sensors from the GUI', https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-iot/organizations/how-to-manage-individual-sensors)
hits.year: 2023 doc (ms.date 2023-01-22, updated 2026-04-28); companion page dated 2026-07-03. Industry documentation, not a paper.
hits.how_close: CLOSEST OPERATIONAL PRECEDENT for time-boxed learning windows. Fetched and verified: the product has Learning, Dynamic and Operational modes. Devices discovered later automatically 'enter learning mode for 7 days'. An admin can put a single Policy Violation alert type back into Learning and 'must enter the length of time, in hours'. When the sensor 'detects significant changes in traffic, it might automatically extend the learning mode'. So the idea of a scoped, time-boxed relearning window already exists in practice and should not be claimed as new. What it does NOT have: no cryptographic binding to a signed OTA, provisioning or config event (only an admin GUI action or unauthenticated device discovery); no slow default budget with a displacement bound; no directional revert. Its triggers are exactly the attack surface the idea closes: an unauthenticated new device gets 7 days of learning, and drift extends learning. That makes it a strong motivating example, not a kill.

hits.title: Data Poisoning Attack against Neural Network-Based On-Device Learning Anomaly Detector by Physical Attacks on Sensors (Ino, Yoshida, Matsutani, Fujino)
hits.how_close: This is the attack the idea cites, not a defense. Fetched: in multi-instance ONLAD, 'a new instance is automatically set' whenever the drift rate theta exceeds theta_drift (2.0 in the experiment). Acoustic injection pushes theta past the threshold and creates a 'poison instance'. The paper proposes no countermeasure: no authorisation, no operator confirmation, no rate limit. It only says countermeasures 'are required'. This confirms that the 'spawn only on a provisioning licence' rule is not already published here.

hits.title: RFC 8520: Manufacturer Usage Description Specification (Lear, Droms, Romascanu)
hits.how_close: CLOSEST STANDARDS PRECEDENT for 'an authenticated vendor statement redefines normal'. Verified: 'A MUD file MUST be signed using CMS'. If signature validation fails, the manager 'MUST cease processing ... until an administrator has given approval'. The MUD URL can travel in an IEEE 802.1AR IDevID/LDevID certificate extension, so it is tied to onboarding identity, which parallels provisioning licences. The file may be refreshed for new communication patterns, and the manager 'SHOULD update the policy expeditiously'. Difference: MUD is a static allow-list or ACL. It does not unlock a learning-rate budget, has no time-box, bound, or revert, and does not handle anomaly-detector poisoning.

hits.conclusion:
The idea is NOT killed by anything I could check, but this kill attempt is INCOMPLETE. The shared WebSearch budget for this turn (200 calls) was already used up, so none of the requested searches ran. I verified candidates only by fetching URLs I already knew (arXiv, RFC Editor, USENIX, JMLR, PMC, Crossref DOI records, Microsoft Learn, Espressif, GitHub). As a result, 2025-2026 coverage is weak: Bose et al. (AISTATS 2025) is the only 2025+ paper. A same-idea 2025-2026 paper could exist and has not been ruled out. To continue the search, send a follow-up message or raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION. Suggested queries: 'maintenance window' or 'change-aware' adaptive anomaly detection with poisoning (2025-2026); OTA or firmware-update concept drift in IoT IDS; MUD with anomaly detection (2024-2026); attestation-gated or authenticated retraining triggers.

What already exists, so do not claim it:
(a) Time-boxed, scoped relearning windows. Microsoft Defender for IoT gives new devices 7 days of learning and offers per-alert Learning set in hours. Its triggers are unauthenticated (device discovery, drift-based extension) or an admin GUI action. This is the closest precedent.
(b) Vendor-signed statements that redefine normal behaviour, bound to onboarding identity: MUD (RFC 8520), with MUD-based monitoring by Hamza et al. 2018/2019. Hamza 2019 says outright that firmware updates make an IDS raise false alarms and force re-identification.
(c) Change-event-aware anomaly analysis in AIOps: Gandalf (NSDI 2020), SCWarn (FSE 2021), LogRobust (FSE 2019).
(d) Trusted provenance to filter poisoning: Baracaldo et al. (AISec 2017, ICIOT 2018). Only metadata was verified; full texts were blocked.
(e) Rate-limited poisoning bounds: Kloft and Laskov (JMLR 2012) and Bose et al. (AISTATS 2025).
(f) Error-triggered fast/slow adaptation: variable forgetting factors (Fortescue et al., 1981).

What appears new within what was checked:
- Binding the adaptation-rate licence cryptographically to a verified OTA, provisioning or config event, scoped to (device_id, fw_hash, K).
- The displacement bound B*t + N_lic*K*B_L*kappa_rev.
- The directional revert at licence end along the threat subspace.
- Spawning new instances only on a provisioning licence. Ino et al. (Sensors 2024) confirm drift-triggered spawning is hijackable and propose no defense.
Pitch the idea as 'authenticated change-management for detector learning', and cite Defender for IoT and MUD as the closest prior art.

Problems found while verifying:
- Mbed TLS does not support Ed25519 (issue #2452 is still open as of Oct 2026). Use ECDSA-P256.
- The original ESP32's Secure Boot V2 is described as RSA-PSS-3072 only.
- Signed-app OTA without hardware Secure Boot does not stop an attacker who can write to flash.

Design gaps to address:
- Token replay. Add a nonce or monotonic counter, and have the gateway attest that the device actually runs fw_hash. Otherwise a valid fleet-wide OTA token can be replayed for a device that never updated.
- Attackers who time their poison to land inside predictable licence windows. Kravchik and Shabtai assume the attacker knows the retraining schedule.
- Attackers who cause legitimate events, for example forcing a factory reset so an admin re-provisions the device. N_lic is then not purely set by the honest event rate.

scores.name: Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA): peers as the drift witness, a signature-free TOA
scores.comment: The 'peers as witness' headline is already CIoTA (NDSS DISS 2018 / JPDC 2020), and LE3D already argues that shared drift is natural and single-device drift is malicious. Robust aggregation plus clipping per client is standard (R-DPFL, BALANCE, ClippedGossip). T2 holds by assumption, since it posits that honest drift is common-mode and contamination reaches at most f streams, so it is not a corollary of WARDEN Thm 15. T1 has an unbudgeted consensus-channel leak (g*C*sigma_idio), which is exactly the surface a frog-boiling attack uses. The biggest practical weakness is that N-BaIoT concurrency is synthetic: the devices were captured separately, so the 'common-mode drift' is drift we inject ourselves, and reviewers will discount that heavily. Vulnerability-diverse peers also push benign vendor-specific drift (a firmware push) into the budget, which opens a liveness gap, and Mirai-style cross-vendor credential botnets break f < |P|/2. Real fleet data would make this stronger, but the 4-6 ESP32 boards running the same telemetry firmware are not a realistic fleet. Better used as a follow-on or a section than as the core paper.

scores.name: Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding: the two-horned attack class on drift-gated defences, with a safety-plus-liveness contract
scores.comment: This has the shape USENIX Security and NDSS reward: a new attack class (deliberately tripping suspicion, rollback or stop gates, then profiting from honest drift after the attacker leaves), measured against published defences, plus a constructive contract and a defence that satisfies it. The static dilemma is pre-empted by CAPTURE Thm 2 and by 2609.23254 Remark 4. Korycki & Krawczyk already describe 'nullifying adaptation' in prose. So the theorem has to be pitched as the adversarial, dynamic, cost-parameterised extension: tau under attacker control, a trip cost c(tau), the post-departure FPR bound 1 - Phi(z_alpha - v*tau/s), and the SAFETY/LIVENESS contract with directional refusal as the positive result. Our strongest asset is the 85-87% vs 0.3% measurement, and this is the candidate that turns it into the headline. It also closes open problem 4. Two risks. First, reimplementing defences on our own PCA-centroid detector invites the straw-man critique, so we must lean on the verified ones with public code or exact rules: OWAD/KitNET, the T2T rollback, the Kloft-Laskov switch-off, the RTTAD stop rule and an EATA filter. We should drop the unverified LID box, CB-RBM and the ACORN stream-inflation claim. Second, the blinding dual is weak as pitched, because WARDEN already concedes tau = +inf as a power loss; it only works as a cost-bounded time-to-blind with a fix. Before writing, we must read AHA's full text and search adversarial CUSUM/QCD, FL framing attacks and squealing/Stick. All of this is CPU-only work on data we already have, so it fits a 2-person team.

scores.name: Rejected-Mode Subspace Budget (RMSB): TOA whose threat directions are learned from the detector's own alarms
scores.comment: Easy to build, since it is one rank-1 projector becoming rank r, but every part has prior art. Kloft & Laskov already use the alarm signal to protect a centroid learner and give the same-shape displacement bound. MINAS/OLINDDA supply the persistent rejected-cluster memory. GPM, SafeGrad and GuardSpace supply the projection. The Thompson thesis anticipates the key observation. Perdisci, Paragraph and Allergy cover decoy and allergy attacks. The theorem holds by construction once the target is already a persistent rejected mode, and the omission attack (no target traffic before compromise) leaves only the backstop. The only real technical content is the persistence-stability lemma. A reviewer would call it an incremental assembly. Its best use is as the signature-free defence inside the gate-tripping paper, and the 'geometry, not rate' contrast with Kloft-Laskov's FPR-triggered freeze is a natural experiment there.

scores.name: Event-Licensed Adaptation: signed firmware and provisioning events unlock a time-boxed fast-learning budget
scores.comment: The headline is already taken. Cisco US9923911B2 raises the learning rate on an event, with scope and schedule. HADES-IoT unlocks re-profiling with a signed command that has replay protection. Defender for IoT ships time-boxed learning windows. Combining these is obvious. The bound has clear holes: replay or downgrade of old tokens, window-timed poisoning, attacker-induced re-provisioning that inflates N_lic, and kappa_rev that holds only inside the known subspace U. The mechanism text also has feasibility errors: mbedTLS has no Ed25519, and the original ESP32 supports only RSA-PSS for Secure Boot V2. Real signed-OTA experiments are achievable, but the security story mostly moves trust into a key-management assumption that reviewers will see as sidestepping the learning problem. Lowest priority.

judged.pick: Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding: the two-horned attack class on drift-gated defences, with a safety-plus-liveness contract
judged.why:
At a top security venue this candidate has the best ratio of what we can claim credibly to how hard it is to build. Its core is an attack the team has already measured and which is unusual: tripping a suspicion gate on purpose drives false alarms to 85-87% after the attacker leaves. Generalising that to published, verified defences closes open problem 4 and gives a clear threat model, an attack algorithm with an explicit trip cost c(tau), a measured break of real systems, and a constructive fix. That fix is the SAFETY/LIVENESS contract, with TOA's directional refusal as the provably good case. All of it runs on the N-BaIoT/Mirai harness we already have, with no new datasets or hardware dependencies.

The other three are mostly assemblies whose headline is pre-empted: FOA by CIoTA and LE3D, RMSB by Kloft-Laskov and MINAS, event-licensing by the Cisco patent and HADES-IoT. FOA also rests on synthetic multi-device concurrency.

Conditions for this to survive review:
1. Frame the theorem as the adversarial, dynamic, cost-bounded extension of CAPTURE Thm 2 and 2609.23254 Remark 4, not as a new impossibility result.
2. Attack only defences whose rules are verified or public: OWAD/KitNET, T2T, RTTAD, EATA, the Kloft-Laskov switch-off, and ASR/Mateen. Drop LID, CB-RBM and the ACORN stream-inflation claim.
3. Recast the blinding dual as a minimum time-to-blind with a direction-weighted radius budget as the fix.
4. Before writing, read AHA and search adversarial CUSUM/QCD, FL framing attacks and squealing.

RMSB is the natural signature-free defence to include in the defence section, and FOA's peer witness can be mentioned as future work for the case where a single stream cannot escape the dilemma.

scores.name: Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA): peers as the drift witness, a signature-free TOA
scores.comment: Of the four, this is the one that makes the ESP32 work matter. Per-device detectors are what actually runs on microcontrollers. A geometric median of 10-float deltas (Weiszfeld, 10 iterations) costs microseconds on an ESP32, and a 40-byte ESP-NOW gossip packet is basically free in radio energy. So a 4-6 board fleet becomes the core experiment, not decoration. It addresses open problems 1, 2 and 3 in one design. Novelty is only incremental: CIoTA already does peer-consensus gating, LE3D already calls common-mode drift natural, and R-DPFL already does robust-aggregate-plus-clip. Two things hold up well enough for a paper: the budgeted residual (where CIoTA simply discards) and vulnerability-diverse peers (where CIoTA uses same-firmware peers), as long as a monoculture-botnet head-to-head against CIoTA shows them. Fixes needed: (a) the T1 leak, by adding a second cumulative budget on the consensus channel; (b) T2 restated as its own multi-stream theorem with fixed f, together with the negative result for victim-only drift; (c) the CIoTA, R-DPFL, WARDEN-gate and Kloft-Laskov baselines. The weak spot is synthetic concurrency on N-BaIoT. CESNET-TimeSeries24 per-IP groups and a real router or endpoint change on the board fleet have to carry the claim that the drift is real.

scores.name: Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding: the two-horned attack class on drift-gated defences, with a safety-plus-liveness contract
scores.comment: This is the most novel empirical angle. Tripping verified gates (T2T rollback, OWAD, RTTAD's stop rule, an EATA-style entropy filter, the Kloft-Laskov switch-off) and measuring liveness after the attacker leaves is something nobody has done, and it closes open problem 4. The theorem, though, is now an extension of CAPTURE Theorem 2 and 2609.23254 Remark 4, not a new result. Several of the six named defences are unverified or don't fit the threat model (LID box, CB-RBM, ACORN-IDS's clean split, DriftXpert's incomplete code), so the defence list shrinks to the ones we can actually confirm. Unsearched areas could still kill it: adversarial quickest-change detection, FL framing attacks, IDS squealing. From a microcontroller point of view the ESP32 part is thin. On-board T2T plus laptop trip bursts is a demo, not a systems contribution. It is mostly a software attack study that would suit a security venue, and it fits best as the attack section inside a defence paper.

scores.name: Rejected-Mode Subspace Budget (RMSB): TOA whose threat directions are learned from the detector's own alarms
scores.comment: The cheapest to build and the cleanest generalisation of TOA: a rank-1 projector becomes rank r, and 8 k-means slots of 10 dims plus Gram-Schmidt on 3 vectors fits easily in ESP32 SRAM. But every part has prior art: Kloft-Laskov alarm-driven protection on the same centroid detector, MINAS persistence, GPM/SafeGrad projection, the Thompson thesis observation, and Perdisci/Allergy decoys. The headline bound follows by construction, and the only real technical content is the persistence-stability lemma. It also only partly addresses open problem 1, since omission attacks fall through to the backstop. It does nothing for the new-device problem and gives the hardware no new role. A good component (FOA's residual projector could be RMSB's subspace), but too weak as the main contribution.

scores.name: Event-Licensed Adaptation: signed firmware and provisioning events unlock a time-boxed fast-learning budget
scores.comment: Hardware-native in spirit (OTA, secure boot, crypto accelerator), but the headline is already covered by the Cisco US9923911B2 fast-learning mode, HADES-IoT's signed re-profiling and Defender for IoT's learning windows. Reviewers will call it an obvious combination. The feasibility claims were wrong (no Ed25519 in mbedTLS; Secure Boot V2 on the original ESP32 is RSA-PSS-3072 only). Burning secure-boot eFuses on our only boards is irreversible and risky for a 2-person student team. The bound needs anti-replay and anti-downgrade assumptions, and kappa_rev < 1 holds only inside the known subspace U. It is also an operational design rather than a research result. Use it at most as a short extension (a licensed join) inside FOA.

judged.pick: Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA): peers as the drift witness, a signature-free TOA
judged.why:
Judged as an IoT systems paper that has to run on real microcontrollers, FOA is the only candidate where the ESP32 fleet is central to the result. Per-device detectors are the natural shape for MCUs. The extra on-device cost (a 10-d geometric median, a 40-byte ESP-NOW gossip packet, HMAC) is small enough to measure and argue for on hardware we already own. It also addresses three of our four open problems with one mechanism:
- drift-hidden attacks, via a multi-stream escape from the single-stream ceiling;
- the 34% false-alarm rate on device join, via a peer-prior bootstrap with a bounded poisoning budget B0+K*B;
- the missing ESP32 evaluation, via a 4-6 board fleet with a real router change as common-mode drift.
It reuses TOA's budget code and proof, the core/ring rule, the N-BaIoT/Mirai harness and the adaptive attacker almost unchanged, so it is feasible for two people.

Novelty is partial, so the paper must be pitched as the first budgeted common/residual update split for label-free detector adaptation. The paper should cite CIoTA, LE3D and R-DPFL up front, and win three ways:
1. A monoculture-botnet scenario where CIoTA's same-firmware consensus absorbs the campaign and FOA's vulnerability-diverse peers do not.
2. Liveness for device-specific benign drift, which CIoTA discards and FOA admits slowly through the budget.
3. A real CESNET-TimeSeries24 common-mode drift result that lifts the single-stream TPR ceiling.

Before writing: close the consensus-channel leak with a second cumulative budget, and restate T2 as a standalone multi-stream theorem with its matching negative result. Gate-Tripping is the runner-up and should not be dropped. Fold its strongest piece, freeze attacks on verified published gates including a CIoTA-style consensus gate and the Kloft-Laskov switch-off, into FOA's evaluation as the attack section. That covers open problem 4 without a second paper.

scores.name: Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA): peers as the drift witness, a signature-free TOA
scores.comment: This is the only candidate that addresses three of our four open problems at once: drift camouflage, the 34% false alarms when a new device joins, and the ESP32 work. The headline idea is not new. CIoTA and LE3D already use peers to tell shared drift from single-device anomalies, so we would have to claim only the budgeted common/residual split, the bounded join and the multi-stream escape, and cite CIoTA first. The work is mostly reuse: the TOA budget code, the core/ring pre-filter and the N-BaIoT/Mirai harness carry over. What is new is the geometric median plus multi-stream plumbing, about one week of work. There are two risks. First, T2 is true almost by assumption, so it has to be stated as its own theorem with a matching negative result, not as a corollary. Second, the T1 consensus-channel leak needs a second budget. Concurrency on N-BaIoT is synthetic, but the ESP32 fleet gives us real common-mode drift, which reviewers in an IoT venue will value. To fit 7 weeks, make CESNET optional and use 4 boards rather than 6.

scores.name: Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding: the two-horned attack class on drift-gated defences, with a safety-plus-liveness contract
scores.comment: Breaking published defences is a strong selling point at security venues, and it closes open problem 4. The theory core is already largely published: CAPTURE Theorem 2, Remark 4 of 2609.23254, and Korycki and Krawczyk's prose on impairing adaptation. That leaves the work resting on the empirical results. Several of the six target defences are unverified (LID box, CB-RBM), have incomplete code (DriftXpert) or have the wrong threat model (ACORN-IDS uses a clean split). Re-implementing them faithfully in 7 weeks, with prior-art searches still to run (adversarial CUSUM, IDS squealing, AHA full text), is a real risk to the schedule. The ESP32 part is decorative, which weakens the 'on-device IoT' story for this course. Better to take its cheapest piece, freeze attacks on the Kloft-Laskov switch-off gate and WARDEN, and use it as a baseline section inside another paper.

scores.name: Rejected-Mode Subspace Budget (RMSB): TOA whose threat directions are learned from the detector's own alarms
scores.comment: The easiest to build: TOA's rank-1 projector becomes rank-r, plus online k-means over alarms. Every component has prior art: Kloft and Laskov use alarms to gate updates, MINAS keeps the persistence memory, and GPM/SafeGrad do the projection. The time-to-compromise bound follows by construction, so the only real theory is the persistence-stability lemma. It does not fix the new-device problem and adds little on ESP32. A reviewer is likely to call it an incremental assembly. It is a good fallback if FOA's multi-stream plumbing slips, and it could fill in for the signature inside FOA's residual channel.

scores.name: Event-Licensed Adaptation: signed firmware and provisioning events unlock a time-boxed fast-learning budget
scores.comment: The headline idea is already covered by the Cisco patent US9923911B2 (event-triggered temporary learning-rate increase with scope), HADES-IoT (signed command unlocks re-profiling) and Defender for IoT's learning windows. The ESP32 path is risky: Secure Boot V2 on the original ESP32 is RSA-PSS only, mbedTLS has no Ed25519, and enabling secure boot burns eFuses irreversibly, which could brick our limited boards. The bound depends on replay, downgrade and attestation assumptions, each of which reviewers would probe. It is mostly systems plumbing with little ML contribution, and it moves away from the poisoning/drift results we already have. The licensed-join idea can be borrowed as a small extension to FOA's join rule.

judged.pick: Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA): peers as the drift witness, a signature-free TOA
judged.why:
FOA scores best on fit (9) and impact (8). It is the only candidate that turns three of our four open problems into contributions:
- attack hidden in drift: the multi-stream escape;
- the 34% new-device false alarms: the bounded peer-prior join;
- ESP32: a multi-board purpose with real common-mode drift.
It also reuses nearly all existing code (TOA budget, core/ring filter, N-BaIoT/Mirai harness, adaptive attacker).

Its novelty is only partial. The claim must be narrowed to "budgeted common/residual update split with a provable time to compromise and a multi-stream escape from the single-stream ceiling". The paper must cite CIoTA, LE3D and R-DPFL up front and beat CIoTA-style same-firmware consensus in a monoculture-botnet scenario.

Seven-week plan:
- W1: multi-stream N-BaIoT harness (cameras + Danmini/Ecobee/Philips) with synthetic common-mode and vendor-specific drift.
- W2: FOA with geometric median, plus a second cumulative budget on the consensus channel to close the T1 leak.
- W3: baselines. CIoTA consensus gating, R-DPFL clipping, WARDEN, a Kloft-Laskov switch-off gate (freeze attack demonstrated on it, a partial answer to open problem 4), TOA and core/ring.
- W4: attacker matrix: f sweep, Sybil, monoculture botnet, core-hiding, attack hidden in drift.
- W5: ESP32 fleet of 4 boards over ESP-NOW. One real router or endpoint change, a laptop poisoner; measure latency, RAM, bytes and energy.
- W6: T1 and T2 proofs, with T2 as a standalone theorem plus its negative result, and ablations.
- W7: writing.
CESNET is a stretch goal only.

Fallbacks:
- If the multi-stream work slips, RMSB is the low-risk option, and its learned subspace can stand in for the signature in FOA's residual channel.
- Gate-Tripping is a better paper later. Its freeze results on published gates make a strong section here, but reproducing six defences faithfully in 7 weeks is too risky, and its theory core is already published.
- Event-Licensed Adaptation is pre-empted by the Cisco patent and HADES-IoT, and the secure-boot eFuse work risks bricking our boards.

ranked: Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding: the two-horned attack class on drift-gated defences, with a safety-plus-liveness contract
Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA): peers as the drift witness, a signature-free TOA
Rejected-Mode Subspace Budget (RMSB): TOA whose threat directions are learned from the detector's own alarms
Event-Licensed Adaptation: signed firmware and provisioning events unlock a time-boxed fast-learning budget
winner: Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding: the two-horned attack class on drift-gated defences, with a safety-plus-liveness contract

final.title: Poison-Resilient On-Device Intrusion Detection for Drifting IoT: Where the 2024-2026 Literature Leaves Us, and the One Direction Worth Building
final.one_line: Make the ESP32 fleet the contribution: a budgeted common-versus-residual update split (Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation) that uses vulnerability-diverse peers to escape the single-stream impossibility results, with freeze attacks on verified published gates as the evaluation section.
final.report_markdown:
> Scope note. This is defensive research: the aim is a detector that keeps protecting constrained IoT devices while an adversary tries to corrupt its self-learning. Attack descriptions are kept at the level a security paper needs to justify a defense, not as operational recipes. All numbers taken from papers read through a summarizing fetch tool are flagged "verify"; check them against the source PDFs before citing.

---

## 1. What the newest research does (2024-2026)

### Theme A: the field now has impossibility theory for self-poisoning

Three 2026 preprints turned "a self-labelling detector slowly poisons itself" from a demo into a proved limit.

- **WARDEN / CDC** (arXiv:2607.21673, 2026, verify) models impurity of a self-updating bank as a generalized Polya urn. The admission-kernel slope `b` behaves like a reproduction number: below 1 impurity settles benign, at or above 1 it goes to full compromise, with a critical contamination rate. Its **Theorem 15** is a two-world construction on a one-dimensional score: honest drift and tail-mimicking contamination can produce the identical unlabelled stream, so any label-free threshold rule that holds a false-alarm rate under drift has detection power capped at `kappa = alpha / (pi + alpha(1-pi))`. A labelled oracle escapes; a single-stream label-free rule cannot.
- **Theory of CL Against Poisoning** (arXiv:2606.29841, ICML 2026, verify) proves no regularized learner converges under frequent shifted poison. Its one-dimensional proof is literally an EMA mean dragged by a persistent bias, which is our centroid. It also contributes the **T2T** rollback defense (flag a task when its score exceeds 2.5x the mean of the last five, then roll back to `w_{t-2}`).
- **CAPTURE** (arXiv:2609.02265, 2026, verify), Theorem 2, gives the static single-statistic dilemma in Le Cam two-point form: any rule reading one statistic has `FUR + RRL >= 1 - delta`, meaning it must either accept injected claims or reject genuine revisions.
- **The Price of Self-Calibration** (arXiv:2609.23254, 2026, verify) gives the non-adversarial version of the same trade-off (Remark 4, "no free tuning"): slowing adaptation narrows the blind set only at the cost of longer miscalibration after legitimate change, and no setting removes both costs. Its blind set for speed-bounded drift is the `2v` class.

Together these say our open problem 1 (an attack hidden inside genuine drift beats the signature-free rule) is **a known impossibility for single-stream label-free learners**, not a bug we can patch within one stream.

### Theme B: published adaptive NIDS and TTA detectors that we can study

- **ACORN-IDS** (arXiv:2602.07291, 2026, verify): continual novelty IDS, PCA reconstruction scorer, threshold `mean + 2*sigma` recomputed per task on a **clean held-out split**. No adversarial analysis. Important correction to our plan: its threshold is not refreshed from stream traffic, so a stream-inflation attack applies only if the clean split or the pseudo-labels can be influenced.
- **DriftXpert** (arXiv:2609.08623, 2026, verify): latent-manifold NIDS with a label-free Outlier Ratio `OR > T` retrain trigger plus selective freezing and weight interpolation. Public code reportedly incomplete (GitHub issue #1). Its OR statistic is essentially our "outer ring gets busier" test, used as a retrain trigger rather than an evidence gate.
- **OWAD** (NDSS 2023, background): calibrator + permutation-test shift detection + explainer + EWC-style consolidated fine-tune. Human labels the selected samples. Public KitNET-on-Kyoto demo. The most natural published defense to attack; its authors list robustness to adversarial attack as future work.
- **CB-RBM / Feature-Context Consistency** (arXiv:2610.16694, NeurIPS 2026, verify): a drift-stable graph fraud detector. Deliberately freezes a drift-invariant score and argues freezing is safe under smooth drift. A frozen plain-RBM baseline there rises to 89-100% false positives under drift, the same effect we measured.
- **RTTAD** (arXiv:2605.10242, 2026, verify) and **Su et al.** (arXiv:2410.04682, ICLR 2025): test-time adaptation that updates only on confident pseudo-normal samples. Su et al. show high-entropy poison is filtered by EATA and design a balanced low-entropy attack to pass the filter; nobody trips the filter to stall adaptation.

### Theme C: attacks on adaptation have matured, but only on the "absorb" side

- **AHA** (CCS 2025 poster, abstract only, verify): reframes boiling-frog with habituation, sensitization, creeping normality, alert fatigue. Conceptual, one VAE/Suricata demo, no measured defense.
- **Korycki & Krawczyk** (Machine Learning 2022): already names, in prose, "impairing the adaptation process" up to "complete nullification", forcing false adaptation, and draining the label budget. Mechanism is masking drift, not tripping a refusal gate; no theorem or contract.
- **Adversarial Attacks for Drift Detection** (ESANN 2025): constructs streams provably invisible to window-based monitors (`W_n v = 0`).
- **Su et al.**, **SuSS 2026** contrastive multi-agent drift induction, and **NDSS 2026** learned pulsing attackers time-boxed to a monitor's refresh windows: all on the absorb or evasion side.

### Theme D: robust statistics and certified updates, all batch or freezing

Online geometric median + Median Covariation Matrix (arXiv:2601.03957, 2026, verify) gives bounded per-point influence but unbounded influence for mean shift and variance inflation (the slow-poison directions), and freezes on long streams (decaying step size, no forgetting). **RPS** (ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.09878) and **LID / Provably Safe Model Updates** (SaTML 2026, arXiv:2512.01899, verify) certify robustness but assume exchangeability or stop updating when the certified box empties.

### Theme E: TinyML on-device learning has no security at all

The ODL survey (arXiv:2605.31226, 2026, verify), about 70 MCU works, contains no poisoning, no adversarial triggering, no IDS, and never mentions ESP32. This is the clearest standing gap.

---

## 2. Honest check: covered versus still new

**Already covered (concede and cite, do not claim):**

| Our element | Covered by | What survives |
|---|---|---|
| Self-poisoning theory (urn, `b` as reproduction number, critical rate) | WARDEN 2026 | We can **measure** `q(rho)` and show `b >= 1` naive, `b < 1` ours; we cannot claim to theorize it first. |
| Open problem 1 (poison inside drift) | WARDEN Thm 15; 2606.29841 Thm 3.1; CAPTURE Thm 2 | Becomes a **corollary**; the contribution must be the side information that escapes the single-stream theorem. |
| "Gradual poisoning of a self-updating NIDS" | AHA (CCS 2025), ANTIDOTE, Kloft & Laskov | Not novel by itself. |
| Core/outer-ring parts | DriftXpert OR (retrain trigger); OWAD/NetSight permutation KL | The assembly and its use as an evidence gate is the thin new part. |
| Adaptive-attacker evaluation | Su et al., ESANN 2025, SuSS 2026, NDSS 2026 | A hand-built "hide in the core" attacker will not satisfy an A/A* reviewer; we need a learned or provably-blind attacker. |

**Still new (defensible):**

1. **TOA as threat-aware rate limiting**: split each update into a signature-direction component (rationed by a slow cumulative budget, giving a provable minimum time to compromise) and the rest (applied in full, never freezes). The nearest relatives restrict updates for other reasons: 2606.29841 penalizes data-covariance eigendirections with no cumulative budget and freezes at `lambda = infinity`; OWAD's consolidation guards forgetting; LID clamps to a static box; EMA and beta-interpolation slow every direction equally. Name it and contrast all four.
2. **The freeze attack as a stated attack surface**: no corpus paper treats a stop-learning, rollback, or gate rule as something an attacker trips on purpose to profit after leaving. Many published defenses have the vulnerable stop-start structure (T2T rollback, DriftXpert/OWAD gates, RTTAD stop rule, EATA filter). This is our most defensible first claim, pending a full read of 2609.23254 and the AHA text.
3. **A joint safety-plus-liveness contract** (minimum time to compromise AND bounded false alarms under honest drift, including after the attacker leaves). No paper states a liveness property for adaptive detectors.
4. **IoT / ESP32 / per-device lifecycle**: no corpus paper runs on an MCU, does per-device self-learning with a safe bootstrap, or treats device churn as an attack vector.
5. **Fleet peers as the side information that escapes the single-stream theorem** (the core of the chosen direction below).

---

## 3. The new direction

### In one paragraph

Keep a per-device centroid detector on every node. The impossibility results all assume **one** score stream, so give each device a second stream: its vulnerability-diverse peers. Each cycle a device proposes an update; the part that a robust peer consensus (geometric median of peers' proposed shifts) backs is applied in full, and only the peer-unexplained residual goes through TOA's slow cumulative budget. Common-mode drift (ISP, gateway, diurnal, campus calendar, a firmware push shared by peers) is applied freely; a single-exploit poisoning campaign, which peers do not share, is rationed. A new device bootstraps from the peer median under the residual budget only, which bounds join-time poisoning and fixes the 34% false-alarm result. We call it **Fleet-Orthogonal Adaptation (FOA)**. The freeze attack, generalized from our own baselines to verified published gates, is the evaluation section: it shows why gating on a single statistic is what FOA avoids.

This is the decisive call. Two of three judges picked FOA over the pure Gate-Tripping paper because FOA makes the ESP32 fleet the contribution (per-device detectors are the natural MCU shape), addresses three of four open problems in one mechanism, and reuses nearly all existing code. Gate-Tripping is the stronger pure-security paper but its theorem core is already published (CAPTURE + 2609.23254) and faithfully reimplementing six defenses in seven weeks is too risky; its strongest piece (freeze attacks on verified gates) folds into FOA's evaluation.

### Exact mechanism (pseudocode)

```
# Per device i, fixed PCA-10 basis frozen after a clean warm-up.
# State: centre c_i (R^10), spread s_i (scalar or per-axis).
# Budget: B0 (initial), B (per-cycle slope). Cumulative residual applied <= B0 + B*t.

for each cycle t:
    x_window = accepted_traffic(i, t)

    # 1. Local proposal via the signature-free core/ring pre-filter
    core      = dense_core(x_window)                 # trimmed inner mass
    ring      = outer_ring(x_window)                 # the periphery
    Delta_i   = proposed_shift(core)                 # centre move from the core only
    dS_i      = proposed_spread_growth(core)

    # 2. Gossip: send Delta_i (10 float32) + HMAC(key_provision) over ESP-NOW / gateway
    broadcast(i, Delta_i, dS_i, hmac=HMAC(key_i, Delta_i || dS_i || t))

    # 3. Peer consensus over the VULNERABILITY-DIVERSE peer group P(i)
    #    (same role + gateway, different vendor/firmware -> a monoculture botnet
    #     cannot fake consensus; network-wide drift is common-mode)
    peers   = verified_peer_shifts(P(i), t)          # drop any failing HMAC
    m_t     = geometric_median(peers, iters=10)      # Weiszfeld; breakdown point 1/2
    mS_t    = geometric_median([dS_j for j in peers])

    # 4. Split into common part + residual
    a_i     = g_i * m_t                              # g_i = per-device gain (warm-up)
    r_i     = Delta_i - a_i

    # 5. Update: common part in full, residual rationed by TWO cumulative budgets
    #    (budget #2 on the consensus channel closes the g*C*sigma leak in T1)
    c_i    += a_i + budget_apply(r_i,  cum_residual,  B0, B)
    c_i    += budget_apply_consensus(a_i, cum_common, B0c, Bc)   # cap on common channel
    # Spread: peer-backed growth in full; device-specific excess budgeted; growth
    # along the signature direction gets a direction-weighted radius budget
    s_i    += peer_backed(mS_t) + budget_apply(excess_spread, cum_spread, ...)

    # 6. Accept/flag using updated (c_i, s_i); self-label accepted traffic as normal

# JOIN: a new device starts from (median peer c, median peer s) and runs its first
# K cycles under the RESIDUAL budget only -> join-time poisoning bounded by B0 + K*B.
```

TOA (the signature-direction budget) is the special case where `P(i)` is empty and the rationed component is the known-signature projection. The signature-free rule is the local pre-filter (`core`, `ring`) that produces `Delta_i`. The freeze attack is what we deliberately avoid: there is no stop-learning gate anywhere, so there is no refusal region for honest drift to trip.

### Why it is different from every recent paper

- **Escapes the impossibility theorems** (WARDEN Thm 15, 2606.29841 Thm 3.1, CAPTURE Thm 2): all are single-stream. FOA's second stream (peers) changes the observation model. In the two-world construction, World-A honest drift is common-mode across peers while World-B contamination reaches at most `f < |P|/2` streams, so a peer-aware rule can hold the false-alarm rate in A and keep detection in B. This must be proved as its **own** multi-stream theorem with fixed `f` (not as a corollary), plus the matching negative result: victim-only drift is still indistinguishable up to rate `B`.
- **Not CIoTA / LE3D** (NDSS DISS 2018, CCNC 2023, the nearest prior art): CIoTA uses same-firmware peers and element-wise consensus and simply **discards** anything without consensus; LE3D only labels common drift natural. FOA (a) uses **vulnerability-diverse** peers so a monoculture botnet cannot manufacture consensus, and (b) **admits the residual slowly through a budget** instead of discarding it, which keeps liveness for device-specific benign drift.
- **Not robust federated aggregation** (R-DPFL 2026, BALANCE CCS 2024): those aggregate one shared model and clip the remainder to zero. FOA keeps per-device models and rations rather than clips, inside a time-to-compromise and freeze analysis.
- **Not T2T / DriftXpert / OWAD / RTTAD / EATA**: all gate adaptation on a statistic, which is exactly the freeze surface; FOA never stops learning.

### How it builds on TOA, the signature-free rule, and the freeze attack

TOA's budget code and minimum-time-to-compromise proof carry over with the signature projector replaced by "residual after consensus". The signature-free core/ring rule becomes the local pre-filter. The freeze attack graduates from our own baselines to published gates and becomes the evaluation that justifies the no-gate design: we show CIoTA-style discard and the gated defenses fail under a tripped-then-left attacker while FOA holds.

---

## 4. Threat model (including an adaptive attacker who knows the defense)

- **Attacker capability**: controls its own traffic on one device and up to `f` peer streams; no gradients, no parameters, no provisioning key (so it cannot forge HMACs or mint peers). Attacker share `rho` of a victim's accepted traffic is the main axis (Kloft & Laskov 2012).
- **Knowledge**: white-box on the algorithm, grey-box on live state. A **surrogate-by-query** attacker rebuilds an approximate centroid from observed accept/flag decisions (Su et al. style), then steers poison.
- **Adaptive attackers to run, each known to the literature**:
  1. Contrastive multi-direction poisoner (SuSS 2026 reward): spreads displacement over mutually dissimilar directions to beat a single budget.
  2. Core-hiding poisoner: matches first and second moments of clean traffic (Su et al. feature-consistency).
  3. Window-blind schedule (ESANN 2025, `W_n v = 0`): provably invisible to our ring windows.
  4. Learned pulsing (NDSS 2026): times bursts to the budget refill.
  5. Monoculture botnet: compromises same-vendor peers to fake consensus (the test that separates FOA from CIoTA).
  6. Omission: withholds attack traffic until after compromise.
- **Failure boundary, reported honestly**: correlated compromise of a majority of the peer group (`f >= |P|/2`), gateway/relay compromise, and cross-vendor credential botnets. State these as the limits where the escape does not hold.

---

## 5. Experiments

### Datasets

- **N-BaIoT (synthesised concurrency)**: Danmini, Ecobee, Philips as vendor-diverse peers, plus the four cameras (Provision PT-737E/PT-838, SimpleHome XCS7-1002/1003). Build time-aligned benign streams; inject (a) common-mode drift (rate/size ramps, gradual mix-in of a second benign profile) and (b) idiosyncratic drift on one device; poison one device toward Mirai scan/ack/syn at `rho` from 5-40%. **Label the concurrency as synthetic**: N-BaIoT captures are per-device and not concurrent (confirmed by the NID dataset survey, Computers & Security 2025, which notes no documented public concept-drift NID dataset existed through 2023).
- **CESNET-TimeSeries24 (real common-mode drift)**: per-IP hourly series, cluster IPs into behavioural peer groups, exploit the real semester-start/holiday shifts as drift speed `v`, inject a boiling-frog ramp toward a scanning profile into one IP. Report detection against WARDEN's `kappa` for single-stream vs FOA to show the ceiling lifts. **Stretch goal**, not on the critical path.
- **ESP32 fleet of 4 (6 if time)**: identical telemetry firmware plus 1-2 different firmwares for diversity, a real router/endpoint change as genuine common-mode drift, a laptop poisoner on one board.

### Baselines (including the newest published defenses)

Naive self-labeller; our freezing baselines; **CIoTA-style same-firmware consensus** (the head-to-head that proves vulnerability diversity); **R-DPFL-style clipped robust aggregation**; **WARDEN frozen reserve + conformal p-values + e-BH**; **Kloft & Laskov switch-off gate** (the classic FPR-triggered freeze, our freeze-attack target); **T2T rollback** and **OWAD** (KitNET public demo) as verified published gates for the freeze section; TOA with a true signature; the signature-free core/ring rule. Drop the unverified LID box and CB-RBM re-implementations and the ACORN stream-inflation claim unless the clean-split threat model is justified.

### Metrics

Time to compromise; FPR during and after the attack plus the half-life of elevated FPR (the liveness metric nobody measures); FPR under honest drift; detection TPR vs WARDEN `kappa`; alerts per device per hour; measured `q(rho)` and `b` per detector (the urn lens); for the freeze section, freeze duty cycle per attacker packet and post-departure FPR validated against the predicted `1 - Phi(z_alpha - v*tau/s)`.

### The one headline figure

A two-panel figure. **Left**: under a monoculture-botnet scenario, CIoTA same-firmware consensus absorbs the campaign (compromise) while FOA's vulnerability-diverse peers hold (100% detection, low FPR). **Right**: post-attacker-departure FPR under honest drift, showing the freezing/gated defenses at the 85-87% false-alarm plateau and FOA flat near its nominal rate. One picture, both the safety win and the liveness win.

### ESP32 measurements

Per-cycle latency; peak RAM including the gossip buffer; ESP-NOW bytes per learning event; energy per learning event via INA219; HMAC verification time. A 10-dimensional geometric median (Weiszfeld, 10 iterations) and a 40-byte gossip packet are cheap enough to measure and defend. Report compute-only power separately from Wi-Fi transmit power (the latter can exceed the TinyML survey's 500 mW class figure).

---

## 6. Runner-up directions worth mentioning

- **Gate-Tripping and Calibration-Blinding** (judge 1's pick): formalize the freeze attack and its dual (blinding a label-free calibrator) as attacks on any suspicion-gated self-learner, with the safety-plus-liveness contract, and break verified published gates on IoT traffic. Strongest pure-security paper, but the theorem core is pre-empted by CAPTURE Thm 2 and 2609.23254 Remark 4, and reproducing six defenses in seven weeks is high-risk. **Use its best piece (freeze attacks on verified gates) as FOA's attack section.**
- **RMSB (Rejected-Mode Subspace Budget)**: TOA whose threat directions are learned from the detector's own alarms (persistent, stationary rejected modes). Cheapest to build (rank-1 projector becomes rank-r), but every part has prior art (Kloft & Laskov alarm-driven protection, MINAS persistence, GPM/SafeGrad projection). **Use as the low-risk fallback and as the learned subspace inside FOA's residual channel.**
- **Event-Licensed Adaptation**: signed firmware/provisioning events unlock a time-boxed fast-learning budget. Headline pre-empted by Cisco US9923911B2, HADES-IoT, and Defender for IoT; secure-boot eFuse burns are irreversible and risky on our only boards. **Borrow only the licensed-join idea as a small extension to FOA's join rule.**

---

## 7. Risks and honest limits

1. **Novelty is partial.** FOA's "peers as witness" headline is CIoTA/LE3D. The paper must be pitched as "the first budgeted common-versus-residual update split for label-free detector adaptation, with a multi-stream escape from the drift/contamination ceiling", citing CIoTA, LE3D, R-DPFL up front, and must beat CIoTA in the monoculture-botnet head-to-head to earn the framing.
2. **Synthetic concurrency on N-BaIoT.** The devices were captured separately, so common-mode drift is injected by us; reviewers discount this. The ESP32 fleet's real router change and CESNET's real calendar drift have to carry the "the drift is real" claim.
3. **Theorem risk.** T2 is almost true by assumption; it must be a standalone multi-stream theorem with fixed `f` plus the victim-only negative result, or reviewers call it a corollary. T1 has an unbudgeted consensus-channel leak (`g*C*sigma_idio`), the exact frog-boiling surface; close it with the second cumulative budget (budget #2 in the pseudocode).
4. **Liveness gap from diversity.** Vulnerability-diverse peers push benign vendor-specific drift (a single-vendor firmware push) into the budgeted residual, which can slow legitimate adaptation. Measure this explicitly.
5. **Must-read-before-writing caveats.** `2609.23254` (manufactured blind sets), Pasikhani et al. TDSC 2026, and the AHA full text are unread and could partly pre-empt framing. Most corpus numbers came through a summarizing fetch tool; verify against PDFs. Several 2026 hits are single-author un-reviewed preprints.
6. **Unsearched kill zones.** Byzantine multi-sensor change detection, federated "framing honest clients" attacks, and classic IDS alert flooding (squealing, Stick/Snot) were not searched and could hide a direct precedent for the freeze section.

---

## 8. Seven-week plan

- **W1**: Multi-stream N-BaIoT harness (cameras + Danmini/Ecobee/Philips) with synthetic common-mode and vendor-specific drift; label synthetic clearly. Read `2609.23254` and the AHA full text.
- **W2**: FOA implemented (geometric median, HMAC gossip, two cumulative budgets to close the T1 leak). Reuse TOA budget code and the core/ring filter unchanged except the projector.
- **W3**: Baselines, CIoTA same-firmware consensus, R-DPFL clipping, WARDEN frozen reserve, the Kloft & Laskov switch-off gate (freeze attack demonstrated on it, closing open problem 4), TOA, signature-free.
- **W4**: Attacker matrix: `f` sweep, Sybil gossip without the key, monoculture botnet, core-hiding, window-blind schedule, a small PPO pulsing attacker, attack-hidden-in-drift. Build the headline figure.
- **W5**: ESP32 fleet of 4 over ESP-NOW: one real router/endpoint change, laptop poisoner, measure latency/RAM/bytes/energy/HMAC time.
- **W6**: T1 and T2 proofs (T2 standalone with its negative result); ablations (plain vs geometric median, peer-group size, `B`, random vs vulnerability-diverse peers, correlated-compromise boundary); measure `q(rho)` and `b`.
- **W7**: Writing. CESNET is a stretch goal only.

**Fallbacks**: if the multi-stream plumbing slips, RMSB is the low-risk core and its learned subspace stands in for the signature in FOA's residual channel. The freeze results on published gates make a strong section regardless of which core ships.

---

### References (10-15 most recent, with role)

1. **WARDEN / CDC** - Self-Poisoning in Adaptive OOD Detection (arXiv:2607.21673, 2026, verify). Role: the impossibility ceiling (Theorem 15, `kappa`) FOA must escape; the urn/`b`-as-reproduction-number lens we measure.
2. **Theory of CL Against Poisoning** (arXiv:2606.29841, ICML 2026, verify). Role: EMA-mean-dragged-by-bias impossibility = our centroid; source of the T2T rollback gate we freeze-attack.
3. **CAPTURE** (arXiv:2609.02265, 2026, verify). Role: static single-statistic dilemma (Thm 2) that our safety-plus-liveness contract extends adversarially; cite, do not restate.
4. **The Price of Self-Calibration** (arXiv:2609.23254, 2026, verify). Role: non-adversarial "no free tuning" trade-off and the `2v` blind set; must read before claiming the freeze framing.
5. **ACORN-IDS** (arXiv:2602.07291, 2026, verify). Role: closest published continual novelty IDS; baseline and attack target; corrects our clean-split assumption.
6. **DriftXpert** (arXiv:2609.08623, 2026, verify). Role: published OR-gated adaptive NIDS; its OR is our ring test; a freeze target with (incomplete) public code.
7. **OWAD** (NDSS 2023). Role: the most natural published defense to freeze-attack; KitNET public demo; evidence that per-device detectors are the practical unit.
8. **CB-RBM / Feature-Context Consistency** (arXiv:2610.16694, NeurIPS 2026, verify). Role: a 2026 "freeze and make the score drift-invariant" design that leaves strategic drift open; contrast for FOA's peer-context idea.
9. **Su et al.** - Adversarial Risk of Test-Time Adaptation (arXiv:2410.04682, ICLR 2025). Role: realistic grey-box/surrogate threat model and the EATA entropy-filter baseline; precedent for our adaptive attacker.
10. **RTTAD** (arXiv:2605.10242, 2026, verify). Role: confident-pseudo-normal TTA with a stop rule; a gated-defense target.
11. **Korycki & Krawczyk** - Adversarial Concept Drift under Poisoning (Machine Learning 2022). Role: prior prose for "impair/nullify adaptation" and label-queue drain; concede that the ideas are not new, draw the distinction.
12. **Kloft & Laskov** - Security Analysis of Online Centroid Anomaly Detection (JMLR 2012). Role: foundation for attacker-share and minimum-time-to-compromise; the classic FPR-triggered switch-off gate we freeze-attack; warns a learned radius invites poisoning.
13. **AHA** - Adversarial Habituation Attack (CCS 2025 poster, verify). Role: newest top-venue naming of boiling-frog / alert fatigue; must read full text before claiming the freeze framing.
14. **CIoTA** - Collaborative IoT Anomaly Detection via Blockchain (NDSS DISS 2018 / JPDC 2020). Role: the closest prior art for peers-as-witness; the head-to-head baseline (same-firmware consensus) FOA must beat with vulnerability diversity.
15. **RPS** - Reliable Prediction Sets under Data Poisoning (ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.09878). Role: two-sided (coverage + size) reliability framing that models our detection-plus-false-alarm contract; background for certified robustness.
